Which two pairings of a PRINCE2 term with the agile term used with it in PRINCE2 Agile are correct?
1. Highlight report and project dashboard.
2. Project product description and product backlog.
3. Project plan and release map.
4. Checkpoint report and burn-up chart.
o: 1 and 2
1 and 3
2 and 4
3 and 4
Agile: Practices & Business Case.w: The project dashboard is used for the highlight report and the release map serves as the project plan, so pairings 1 and 3 are correct (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 12.1, 8.3.2.5).

n.0: Pairing 2 is wrong: the project product description is tailored into the project backlog, not the product backlog (book 8.3.2.1).
n.2: Pairing 2 is wrong (project backlog, not product backlog) and pairing 4 is wrong (the checkpoint report pairs with the team dashboard) (book 8.3.2.1, Table 12.1).
n.3: Pairing 4 is wrong: a burn-up chart may appear on a dashboard, but the checkpoint report is replaced by the team dashboard (book Table 12.1).

Agile: Practices & Business Case.q: Which PRINCE2 Agile role is described as a version of the PRINCE2 team manager role?
o: Team coach
Chief product owner
Agile coach
Product owner
Agile: Practices & Business Case.w: The product owner is a version of the team manager: the PM agrees work with the PO, who owns the team's product backlog and has direct authority over the delivery team (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 7.3.1, Table 7.2).

n.0: The team coach helps one or two teams to self-manage (a Scrum master fits here); it is not the team manager equivalent (book Table 7.2).
n.1: The chief product owner represents users and sets priorities across teams at project level, not as a team manager (book Table 7.2).
n.2: The agile coach works across the organization to remove systemic blockers; it is not a team-level management role (book Table 7.2).

Agile: Practices & Business Case.q: In PRINCE2 Agile, which artifact tailors the PRINCE2 project product description?
o: Product backlog
Project canvas
Project backlog
Release map
Agile: Practices & Business Case.w: The project backlog replaces the project product description: it holds high-level, mostly epic, user stories and shows or links to the project DoR and DoD (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 8.3.2.1).

n.0: The product backlog is the team-level backlog that tailors product descriptions and links to the team DoD (book 8.3.2.1).
n.1: The project canvas tailors the business case, not the project product description (book 6.3.2.1).
n.3: The release map tailors the project and stage plans (book 8.3.2.5).

Agile: Practices & Business Case.q: Which statement about terminology in PRINCE2 Agile is correct?
o: Agile terms such as 'user story' are used alongside PRINCE2 terms such as 'product description'
PRINCE2 terms are kept and agile terms are avoided, so that governance stays consistent
Agile terms replace PRINCE2 terms, so management product names are dropped from the method
A new shared vocabulary is agreed in the project initiation workshop before any terms are used
Agile: Practices & Business Case.w: Because there is no common terminology, PRINCE2 Agile uses a mixture of both, pairing PRINCE2 terms with agile ones such as product description and user story (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 5.8).

n.1: PRINCE2 Agile does not avoid agile terms; it combines them with PRINCE2 terms (book 5.8).
n.2: Management products are kept or tailored and still named; the book combines terms rather than replacing them (book 5.8).
n.3: The book's answer to the terminology gap is to combine existing terms, not to create a new vocabulary in a workshop (book 5.8, Table 13.7).

Agile: Practices & Business Case.q: How can the business case practice keep the work of an agile project focused on value?
o: By delivering every feature in one final release, so that the full benefits arrive together at closure
By assigning a value to each user story and prioritizing the work by its value against the objective
By replacing the business case with the product backlog once the first iteration has started
By measuring the velocity of each team and directing the most funding to the fastest team
Agile: Practices & Business Case.w: PRINCE2 Agile asks that every effort contributes to meaningful outcomes; a practical way is to give each user story a value and prioritize by value against the objective (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 6.3.1).

n.0: Agile delivers incrementally and plans frequent releases so benefits arrive early; holding everything for one final release works against the value focus (book 6.3.1, Table 6.1).
n.2: All projects still need business justification; the business case is tailored (for example into a project canvas), not replaced by a backlog (book 6.3.1, 6.3.2).
n.3: Velocity is a planning measure of how much a team completes; it does not express the value of the work to the business (book 8.3, 6.3.1).

Agile: Practices & Business Case.q: What is the main purpose of a minimum viable product (MVP) in PRINCE2 Agile?
o: To provide the complete, fully tested product that is handed over at project closure
To define the lowest quality standard that the users will accept for every product
To build a basic version of the product cheaply and quickly to gather early feedback
To set the largest scope that can be delivered within the agreed project budget
Agile: Practices & Business Case.w: An MVP is a basic version built with minimal cost and time so that core features and assumptions can be tested and feedback gathered early; it is then refined from that feedback (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 6.3.1).

n.0: An MVP is not a finished product; it is an early version that is refined from user feedback (book 6.3.1).
n.1: Quality criteria are set through the quality practice and the DoD; the MVP is about testing core features cheaply, not about a quality floor (book 6.3.1, 9.3.2).
n.3: The MVP is the smallest useful version of the product, not the largest scope affordable within the budget (book 6.3.1).

Agile: Practices & Business Case.q: In the PRINCE2 Agile default approach to fixing and flexing the aspects of project performance, how is the benefits aspect treated?
o: It has zero tolerance on every level of plan, in the same way as time and cost
It is fixed for the Must haves and flexed for the Should haves and Could haves
It is fixed for the minimum criteria and flexed above the minimum criteria
It is fixed for minimum viability and flexed above minimum viability
Agile: Practices & Business Case.w: Benefits are fixed at the level of minimum viability and may be flexed above that level, so the project must at least deliver a viable level of benefit (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 3.1).

n.0: Zero tolerance at all levels of plan is the default for time and cost, not benefits (book Table 3.1).
n.1: Fixed for Must haves and flexed for Should and Could haves is the default for scope (book Table 3.1).
n.2: Fixed for minimum criteria and flexed above them is the default for sustainability; benefits use minimum viability (book Table 3.1).

Agile: Practices & Business Case.q: Where an MVP is used, why must it be identified in the business case (project canvas) of a PRINCE2 Agile project?
o: So that an exception can be raised if it is forecast to be delivered late
So that the team coach can schedule it into the first team retrospective
So that the users know which features will be left out of the final product
So that the chief product owner can remove it from the project backlog
Agile: Practices & Business Case.w: If an MVP is used, the business case must identify it so that an exception can be raised when its delivery is forecast to be later than expected (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 6.1).

n.1: Retrospectives review how the team works; the MVP is identified in the business case to support exception management (book Table 6.1).
n.2: The MVP describes what is delivered first, not what is excluded from the final product (book 6.3.1).
n.3: The MVP's features are delivered, not removed; it is named in the business case so late delivery can trigger an exception (book Table 6.1).

Agile: Practices & Business Case.q: A team is developing a highly innovative product whose success rests on several untested assumptions. How should it approach its MVP?
o: Use the MVP to explore the key assumptions and validate them as quickly as possible
Delay the MVP until detailed upfront design has removed the main uncertainties
Define the MVP once during starting up and keep it unchanged to protect the benefits
Treat the MVP as the full project scope and extend the timescale to deliver it
Agile: Practices & Business Case.w: How an MVP is defined depends on uncertainty; in highly innovative contexts it often means exploring key assumptions and validating them as fast as possible (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 6.3.1).

n.1: Waiting for upfront design defeats the purpose of an MVP, which tests assumptions early with minimal investment (book 6.3.1).
n.2: An MVP is refined using feedback; freezing it ignores what is learned from testing the assumptions (book 6.3.1).
n.3: An MVP is a minimal version, not the full scope, and time has zero tolerance by default, so the timescale is not extended (book 6.3.1, Table 3.1).

Agile: Practices & Business Case.q: Which statement about business justification in a PRINCE2 Agile project is correct?
o: Agile projects deliver value continuously, so a formal business justification becomes optional
The business case can be tailored, for example into a project canvas, but justification is still needed
Business justification is checked once, at the end of initiation, and then passed to the CPO to own
The product backlog replaces the business case because each user story carries its own value
Agile: Practices & Business Case.w: All projects must have business justification. PRINCE2 Agile tailors the business case, for example into a project canvas, rather than removing it (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 6.3.1, Table 6.1).

n.0: Business justification is never dropped; PRINCE2 Agile tailors how it is documented (book 6.3.1).
n.2: The business case is checked throughout the project, including at stage boundaries and closure, not once at initiation (book 6.3.1, Table 13.4).
n.3: Assigning value to stories supports the value focus, but the backlog does not replace the business case; the project canvas does (book 6.3.1, 6.3.2.1).

Agile: Practices & Business Case.q:
Which two statements about the MVP in PRINCE2 Agile are correct?
1. It is a basic version of the product built with minimal cost and time.
2. It is the finished product that is handed over to operations at closure.
3. It allows core product features to be tested with minimal investment.
4. It contains every Must have and Should have requirement in the project backlog.
o: 1 and 2
2 and 4
1 and 3
3 and 4
Agile: Practices & Business Case.w: An MVP is a basic version built quickly and cheaply (1) that lets core features be tested with minimal investment (3) (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 6.3.1).

n.0: Statement 2 is wrong: an MVP is an early version refined by feedback, not the finished product (book 6.3.1).
n.1: Statements 2 and 4 describe a complete product; an MVP is minimal and early (book 6.3.1).
n.3: Statement 4 is wrong: an MVP holds the essential features, not every Must have and Should have (book 6.3.1).

Agile: Practices & Business Case.q: A project board asks why the teams are building the highest-value user stories first. Which explanation best reflects the business case practice in PRINCE2 Agile?
o: It means the board no longer needs to set time and cost tolerances for the project
It allows the team to skip the MVP when the first stories are well received by users
It means the project backlog no longer needs a project Definition of Done
If time runs out, the features left undelivered are those of least value to the business
Agile: Practices & Business Case.w: Work is prioritized by value, and with time and cost fixed it is lower-priority scope that flexes, so whatever is left out when time runs out is of least value (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 6.3.1, Table 3.1).

n.0: Time and cost still carry tolerances (zero by default); prioritizing by value does not remove them (book Table 3.1).
n.1: Prioritizing by value does not remove the MVP; an MVP tests core features early with minimal investment (book 6.3.1).
n.2: The project DoD is still needed to say when work is acceptable; it is set in the project initiation workshop (book Table 13.7).

Agile: Practices & Business Case.q: When the outline project canvas is being produced, the team explores the available business options and gathers the information needed to support an investment decision. Which step of the business case technique is this?
o: Check
Confirm
Maintain
Develop
Agile: Practices & Business Case.w: The develop step explores options and obtains the right information for investment appraisal decisions, which in an agile project means considering business value and benefits while producing the project canvas (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 6.3.1, Figure 6.3).

n.0: Check assesses whether a project already under way is still worthwhile; it does not create the first view of the options (book 6.3.1).
n.1: Confirm assesses whether the intended benefits have been or will be realized, mostly after closure (book 6.3.1).
n.2: Maintain keeps an existing business case up to date with progress and forecasts; exploring the initial options is the develop step (PRINCE2 7 manual 5.3.1).

Agile: Practices & Business Case.q:
Identify the missing word in the following sentence.
In the business case technique, the [?] step assesses whether the project is still worthwhile.
o: check
develop
confirm
maintain
Agile: Practices & Business Case.w: The check step asks whether the project is (still) worthwhile, supporting the principle of ensuring continued business justification (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 6.3.1, Figure 6.3).

n.1: Develop explores options and gathers information for the initial investment decision (book 6.3.1).
n.2: Confirm assesses whether the intended benefits have been or will be realized (book 6.3.1).
n.3: Maintain updates the business case with actuals and forecasts; judging whether it is still worthwhile is the check step (PRINCE2 7 manual 5.3.1).

Agile: Practices & Business Case.q: When does the confirm step of the business case technique mostly take place, and why can part of it happen earlier in a PRINCE2 Agile project?
o: Before initiation, because the project mandate already states the expected benefits in full
Mostly after closure, but releasing products iteratively can realize some benefits during the project
At each daily stand-up, because every completed user story carries a benefit that can be confirmed
At the end of initiation, because the full project canvas is approved by the board at that point
Agile: Practices & Business Case.w: Confirming benefits mostly happens after the project closes, but because agile releases products iteratively, some benefits may be realized and confirmed during the project (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 6.3.1).

n.0: Benefits cannot be confirmed before anything is delivered; the mandate only triggers starting up (book 6.3.1, Table 13.1).
n.2: Stand-ups coordinate daily work; benefits are measurable improvements from outcomes and are confirmed through benefits reviews, not story by story (book 6.3.1, Table 6.1).
n.3: Approving the full project canvas authorizes the project; it confirms the justification, not that benefits have been realized (book Table 13.4, 6.3.1).

Agile: Practices & Business Case.q: In the 'prepare the outline business case' activity of starting up a project, who leads the team in developing the project canvas from the project mandate?
o: The project manager
The chief product owner
The project executive
The senior supplier
Agile: Practices & Business Case.w: The project executive leads development of the project canvas from the mandate; the project manager, consulting the CPO, senior supplier and executive, then defines what is to be delivered and creates the project backlog (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.1).

n.0: The project manager creates the project backlog in this activity, but the executive leads the project canvas (book Table 13.1).
n.1: The CPO is consulted on what is to be delivered and owns the project backlog; the executive leads the canvas (book Table 13.1, Table 7.2).
n.3: The senior supplier is consulted when the project backlog is defined; the executive leads the canvas (book Table 13.1).

Agile: Practices & Business Case.q: What happens to the business case in the 'prepare the full business case' activity of initiating a project?
o: The project manager seeks lessons on business case development and creates a more detailed project canvas
The chief product owner converts the outline project canvas into epics in the project backlog
The project board confirms that the expected benefits have been realized by the first release
The project canvas is baselined in the PID so that it is not updated again until project closure
Agile: Practices & Business Case.w: In initiation the project manager, with the project team, draws on lessons about business case development and produces a more detailed project canvas for the board's authorization (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.6).

n.1: The project backlog of epics is created in starting up; it does not replace the business case (book Table 13.1, 6.3.1).
n.2: Nothing has been released during initiation, so there are no realized benefits to confirm (book 6.3.1).
n.3: The canvas continues to be updated, for example at stage boundaries, so that business justification is checked throughout (book 6.3.1, 13.7.4.1).

Agile: Practices & Business Case.q: What does the project board do with the project canvas during the 'authorize project closure' activity?
o: It creates a new project canvas for the next project
It hands the project canvas to the product owners to maintain
It replaces the project canvas with the lessons report
It confirms the updated project canvas
Agile: Practices & Business Case.w: When authorizing closure, the board compares the original and current PID, approves the end project report, makes sure post-project benefits reviews are planned and confirms the updated project canvas (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.4).

n.0: A new canvas would be developed in starting up a new project; at closure the board confirms this project's updated canvas (book Table 13.1, Table 13.4).
n.1: Product owners own team product backlogs; the canvas is confirmed by the board, and later benefits are covered by post-project reviews (book Table 13.4, Table 7.2).
n.2: The lessons report records lessons for the future; it does not replace the business justification in the project canvas (book Table 13.18, Table 13.4).

Agile: Practices & Business Case.q:
Which two statements about the business case technique in a PRINCE2 Agile project are correct?
1. The project canvas is first produced in starting up and is developed in more detail during initiation.
2. Once the project is authorized, the project canvas is not reviewed again until closure.
3. Releasing products iteratively can allow some benefits to be confirmed during the project.
4. The confirm step takes place once, during the project closure workshop.
o: 1 and 2
2 and 4
1 and 3
3 and 4
Agile: Practices & Business Case.w: The canvas is developed in starting up and refined in initiation (1), and iterative releases can let some benefits be confirmed before closure (3) (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 6.3.1, Table 13.1, Table 13.6).

n.0: Statement 2 is wrong: the canvas is reviewed throughout, for example in release planning and at stage boundaries, to check continued business justification (book 6.3.1, 13.7.4.1).
n.1: Statement 2 is wrong (the canvas is reviewed throughout) and statement 4 is wrong (confirming benefits mostly happens after closure, through post-project reviews) (book 6.3.1).
n.3: Statement 4 is wrong: confirmation of benefits mostly takes place after the project has closed, not once in the closure workshop (book 6.3.1, Table 13.4).

Agile: Practices & Business Case.q: Why does a PRINCE2 Agile project keep checking its business case as releases are delivered, rather than checking it once at the start?
o: The chief product owner must re-approve every user story against the project canvas before it is built
Feedback and releases can change the costs, value and benefits, so the project must stay worthwhile throughout
Time and cost tolerances are reset at every iteration, so the business case must be rewritten to match
The project canvas is replaced by the product backlog after the first release, so it needs a final check
Agile: Practices & Business Case.w: The business case is checked to confirm that the project remains worthwhile as new information emerges, in line with ensuring continued business justification (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 6.3.1).

n.0: The CPO prioritizes the project backlog; repeated checks of the business case are about justification, not approving each story (book Table 7.2, 6.3.1).
n.2: Time and cost have zero tolerance by default at all levels of plan; they are not reset each iteration (book Table 3.1).
n.3: The project canvas remains the business case for the whole project and is confirmed at closure (book 6.3.2.1, Table 13.4).

Agile: Practices & Business Case.q: What is the project canvas in PRINCE2 Agile?
o: A one-page visual artifact that sets out the project and its business justification
A visual plan that clusters user stories into releases of two to four iterations each
A visual board of team progress, updated in team planning and retrospective workshops
A prioritized list of epic user stories that replaces the project product description
Agile: Practices & Business Case.w: The project canvas is a one-page visual tailoring of the business case: it summarizes the project and documents its business justification (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 6.3.2.1, Glossary).

n.1: Clustering user stories into releases describes the release map, which serves as the project and stage plan (book 8.3.2.5).
n.2: A board of team progress updated in team planning and retrospectives is the team dashboard (book Table 12.1).
n.3: A list of epics replacing the project product description is the project backlog (book 8.3.2.1).

Agile: Practices & Business Case.q: Which set of elements does the PRINCE2 Agile project canvas contain?
o: Project vision, OKRs, team values, skill matrix, users, scope, costs and benefits
Project vision, business value, business options, costs, users, scope, benefits and major risks
Epics, user stories, Definition of Ready, Definition of Done, velocity, risks, issues and costs
Benefits realization procedures, measurement and tolerance guidance, responsibilities and tools
Agile: Practices & Business Case.w: The suggested PRINCE2 Agile project canvas holds eight elements: project vision, business value, business options, costs, users, scope, benefits and major risks (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 6.3.2.1, Glossary).

n.0: OKRs are defined in release planning, and team values and the skill matrix are kickoff workshop topics; none are canvas elements (book Table 13.16, Table 13.8).
n.2: Epics, user stories, DoR and DoD belong to the backlogs and the quality practice, not the canvas (book 8.3.2.1, 9.3.2).
n.3: Realization procedures, measurement and tolerance guidance, responsibilities and tools are contents of the benefits management approach (book Table 6.1).

Agile: Practices & Business Case.q: Which workshop, held during starting up a project, has topics including user group definition, business option selection, benefits analysis and cost definition?
o: Starting up workshop
Project initiation workshop
Project canvas workshop
Release planning workshop
Agile: Practices & Business Case.w: The project canvas workshop builds a shared understanding of the project's core elements; its topics include user group definition, business option selection, project vision, benefits, risk, scope, cost and business value definition (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 13.2.4.1, Table 13.2).

n.0: The starting up workshop covers project roles, lessons review, initiation stage planning, risk analysis and refine planning (book Table 13.3).
n.1: The project initiation workshop, in initiating a project, covers the Agilometer, management approaches, project DoR and DoD, personas, release planning and canvas refinement (book Table 13.7).
n.3: The release planning workshop covers introduction, OKR definition, release planning and wrap-up (book Table 13.16).

Agile: Practices & Business Case.q: An agile pilot project's draft project canvas lists 'an agile transformation plan' under benefits. Why is this incorrect?
o: The plan is a response to agile adoption risk, so it belongs under major risks
The plan is a cost incurred by the business, so it belongs under costs instead
The plan is a management product, so it belongs in the PID rather than the canvas
The plan is an output of the project, so it belongs under scope rather than benefits
Agile: Practices & Business Case.w: A benefit is a measurable improvement resulting from an outcome; a plan the project produces is an output, which the canvas records under scope (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Glossary, 6.3.2.1, Figure 6.3).

n.0: Major risks on the canvas are uncertainties that could affect the project; a deliverable plan is an output, recorded under scope (book 6.3.2.1).
n.1: Costs record what the project will spend; the plan itself is something the project delivers, so it is scope (book 6.3.2.1).
n.2: When a pilot produces the plan as a deliverable it is an output of the project, so it is shown under the canvas scope (book 6.3.2.1, Glossary).

Agile: Practices & Business Case.q: How does the project canvas document the business justification for a PRINCE2 Agile project?
o: By comparing each delivery team's velocity with the dates shown on the release map
By weighing estimated costs against expected benefits and value, offset by the risks
By recording the acceptance criteria and test results for each user story delivered
By listing the quality register entries for each release and their review outcomes
Agile: Practices & Business Case.w: The canvas documents business justification by setting estimated costs against expected benefits and value, offset by the risks involved (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 6.1).

n.0: Velocity and the release map are planning tools; they forecast delivery but do not justify the investment (book 8.3, 8.3.2.5).
n.2: Acceptance criteria and test results belong to the quality practice, not the business justification (book 9.3).
n.3: Quality register entries record quality activities and results; they do not document why the investment is worthwhile (book Table 9.1).

Agile: Practices & Business Case.q: When the business case is tailored into a project canvas, which scenarios should the canvas outline?
o: Best-case, worst-case and expected-case scenarios
Must have, Should have and Could have scenarios
Current-state, transition-state and target-state scenarios
Threat, opportunity and secondary-risk scenarios
Agile: Practices & Business Case.w: PRINCE2 Agile tailors the business case into the project canvas, which should outline best-case, worst-case and expected-case scenarios (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 5.2).

n.1: Must, Should and Could are MoSCoW priorities used for scope, not business case scenarios (book Table 3.1).
n.2: Current and target states describe organizational change in OCM, not business case scenarios (book 4.2.1).
n.3: Threats and opportunities are risk categories recorded through the risk practice, not canvas scenarios (book 10.1, Table 13.3).

Agile: Practices & Business Case.q: After starting up a project, how is the project canvas developed further in PRINCE2 Agile?
o: It is replaced by the project initiation documentation once initiation begins
It is split so that each product owner keeps a separate canvas for their own team
It is frozen at the end of starting up so that the benefits can no longer be flexed
It is refined in the project initiation workshop and reviewed again in release planning
Agile: Practices & Business Case.w: Project canvas refinement is a topic of the project initiation workshop, and the release planning workshop reviews the project canvas with the project backlog and release map (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.7, 13.7.4.1).

n.0: The detailed canvas is shared with the board alongside the PID when authorization is requested; it is not replaced (book Table 13.6).
n.1: There is one project canvas for the project; product owners own team product backlogs (book 6.3.2.1, Table 7.2).
n.2: The canvas keeps being refined and checked; benefits are fixed only at minimum viability and can flex above it (book Table 13.7, Table 3.1).

Agile: Practices & Business Case.q: In the scope definition topic of the project canvas workshop, how is the project's scope typically expressed?
o: As detailed tasks estimated in hours for each developer
As user stories for the first iteration, ready for the team plan
As epics prioritized using MoSCoW, with a timeline and tolerance
As product register entries for each specialist product
Agile: Practices & Business Case.w: Scope definition in the project canvas workshop sets a timeline and tolerance and expresses scope as epics prioritized with MoSCoW (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.2).

n.0: Task-level planning is done only for the next iteration in managing product delivery, not in starting up (book Table 8.1, Table 13.12).
n.1: Detailed user stories for an iteration are prepared in team planning during managing product delivery (book 13.6.4.1).
n.3: The product register records products and their status during the project; scope on the canvas is high-level epics (book Table 9.1, Table 13.2).

Agile: Practices & Business Case.q: In a PRINCE2 Agile project, what does the project brief outline that reflects the agile way of working?
o: The detailed task-level team plan for each iteration in the first stage
The signed-off list of user stories for the whole of the project
The flexible areas of scope and quality criteria, based on prioritization
The velocity that each delivery team is required to achieve per iteration
Agile: Practices & Business Case.w: In PRINCE2 Agile the project brief outlines which areas of scope and quality criteria are flexible, based on prioritization, and describes the agile techniques and approaches chosen with their expected benefits (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 6.1).

n.0: Team plans are produced by the delivery team for the next iteration during managing product delivery, not in the project brief (book Table 8.1).
n.1: Agile expects requirements to evolve; a fixed, signed-off list of all stories contradicts the flexible scope the brief describes (book Table 6.1).
n.3: Velocity is measured from the team's actual work and used to forecast; it is not imposed through the brief (book 8.3).

Agile: Practices & Business Case.q: Why does the project brief in a PRINCE2 Agile project include more detailed information about operations and maintenance than a traditional brief might?
o: Incremental delivery means products reach operational use during the project
The operations team takes ownership of the project backlog during initiation
Maintenance costs are the performance aspect that flexes instead of scope
The project brief replaces the benefits management approach in agile
Agile: Practices & Business Case.w: Because agile delivers incrementally, products go into operational use before the project ends, so the brief gives more detail on how this affects operations and maintenance (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 6.1).

n.1: The project backlog is owned by the chief product owner, not the operations team (book Table 7.2).
n.2: Cost has zero tolerance by default; scope (Should and Could haves) is what flexes (book Table 3.1).
n.3: The benefits management approach is still used in PRINCE2 Agile; the brief does not replace it (book Table 6.1).

Agile: Practices & Business Case.q: In a PRINCE2 Agile project, which management product plans frequent releases so that benefits are delivered early to users or customers?
o: Project brief
Commercial management approach
Quality management approach
Benefits management approach
Agile: Practices & Business Case.w: In PRINCE2 Agile the benefits management approach plans frequent releases to enable early delivery of benefits, as well as defining benefits management actions and reviews (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 6.1).

n.0: The project brief outlines flexible scope and quality areas and the agile techniques chosen; it is not where benefit-enabling releases are planned (book Table 6.1).
n.1: The commercial management approach makes procurement and contracts support agile delivery, for example fixed team costs per iteration (book Table 7.3).
n.2: The quality management approach covers quality standards, agile testing and responsibilities, not the timing of benefits (book Table 9.1).

Agile: Practices & Business Case.q: Which content belongs in the benefits management approach of a PRINCE2 Agile project?
o: Project vision, business options, users, costs and the major risks of the project
Benefits realization procedures, measurement and tolerance guidance, and responsibilities
Flexible areas of scope and quality, and the agile techniques chosen for the project
Fixed delivery team costs per iteration, the MVP and an agreed Definition of Done
Agile: Practices & Business Case.w: The benefits management approach typically covers realization procedures, measurement and tolerance guidance, responsibilities, resources, tools and techniques, standards and references (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 6.1).

n.0: Vision, business options, users, costs and major risks are elements of the project canvas (book 6.3.2.1).
n.2: Flexible scope and quality areas and the chosen agile techniques are described in the project brief (book Table 6.1).
n.3: Fixed team costs per iteration, the MVP definition and an agreed DoD are examples of what the commercial management approach supports (book Table 7.3).

Agile: Practices & Business Case.q: What is the purpose of the sustainability management approach that a PRINCE2 Agile project agrees in initiating a project?
o: To define the benefits management actions and the reviews that confirm benefits are realized
To make sure that procurement and contracts support agile product development
To record the threats and opportunities to the project and the status of each
To define the actions, reviews and controls needed to meet the sustainability performance targets
Agile: Practices & Business Case.w: The sustainability management approach, a PRINCE2 Project Management product used in PRINCE2 Agile, defines the actions, reviews and controls for achieving the project's sustainability performance targets; it is agreed with the other management approaches in initiation (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.6; PRINCE2 7 business case practice).

n.0: Benefits management actions and benefits reviews are defined in the benefits management approach (book Table 6.1).
n.1: Making procurement and contracts support agile delivery is the commercial management approach (book Table 7.3).
n.2: Recording identified risks and their status is the role of the risk register (book Table 10.1).

Agile: Practices & Business Case.q: A cheaper supplier offers to cut project costs but cannot meet the project's minimum sustainability criteria. What does the PRINCE2 Agile default for the sustainability aspect suggest?
o: Accept the offer, because cost is fixed and sustainability is a flexed aspect
Accept the offer, because the CPO may trade sustainability against benefits
Reject the offer, because sustainability is fixed at its minimum criteria
Reject the offer, because sustainability has zero tolerance at every level
Agile: Practices & Business Case.w: Sustainability is fixed for its minimum criteria and flexed only above them, so a supplier that cannot meet the minimum is not acceptable; scope is flexed instead (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 3.1).

n.0: Cost is fixed, but sustainability is flexed above its minimum criteria and fixed at them, which this offer would breach (book Table 3.1).
n.1: The minimum sustainability criteria are fixed; they are not traded against other aspects (book Table 3.1).
n.3: Zero tolerance at every level of plan is the default for time and cost; sustainability can be flexed above its minimum (book Table 3.1).

Agile: Practices & Business Case.q: When the project board authorizes initiation, which management product does it approve together with the release map for initiation?
o: Project initiation documentation
Project brief
Benefits management approach
Sustainability management approach
Agile: Practices & Business Case.w: In 'authorize initiation' the board approves the project brief and the release map for initiation, then authorizes the project manager to start initiating the project (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.4).

n.0: The PID is assembled during initiation and approved later, when the board authorizes the project (book Table 13.4).
n.2: The benefits management approach is agreed during initiating a project, so it does not yet exist when initiation is authorized (book Table 13.6).
n.3: The sustainability management approach is agreed during initiating a project, after initiation has been authorized (book Table 13.6).

Agile: Practices & Business Case.q: Which statement about the benefits management approach in a PRINCE2 Agile project is correct?
o: It should cover how benefits that arise after closure will be confirmed
It is replaced by the benefits element of the project canvas in agile
It is first created in closing a project to record benefits achieved
It defines the quality criteria and acceptance methods for products
Agile: Practices & Business Case.w: Benefits often arise after the project ends, so closing a project checks that the benefits management approach includes post-project benefit confirmation, and the board ensures post-project benefits reviews are planned (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.18, Table 13.4).

n.1: The canvas lists the expected benefits, but the benefits management approach is still used to define benefits actions and reviews (book Table 6.1).
n.2: It is agreed in initiating a project with the other management approaches; closing only checks it covers post-project reviews (book Table 13.6, Table 13.18).
n.3: Quality criteria and acceptance methods belong to the quality practice and its products (book 9.1).

Agile: Practices & Business Case.q: Why are personas useful when developing the business case for a PRINCE2 Agile project?
o: They give a clear overview of each team member's skills, strengths and gaps so training can be planned
They help identify and articulate the specific benefits the project can deliver to its users and stakeholders
They set out how much authority the board delegates to the teams for each type of key decision
They track the total level of risk exposure across iterations so that trends can be monitored
Agile: Practices & Business Case.w: Personas help a project identify and articulate the specific benefits it can deliver to users, customers and stakeholders, which is why they sit in the business case practice (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 6.4.1).

n.0: An overview of team skills, strengths and gaps is the team skill matrix in the organization practice (book 7.4.1).
n.2: Agreeing levels of delegated authority for decisions is done with delegation poker and the delegation matrix (book 7.4.3).
n.3: Tracking total risk exposure across iterations is the cumulative risk burn-down chart in the risk practice (book 10.4.2).

Agile: Practices & Business Case.q: How does PRINCE2 Agile recommend that personas are created?
o: By the chief product owner, working from market research before initiation
By project support, using the stakeholder analysis in the communication approach
By the project executive, as part of the project mandate from the business
By a cross-functional group in a workshop that includes development team members
Agile: Practices & Business Case.w: Personas should be written collaboratively in a cross-functional workshop with development team members, so the people building the product share the understanding of users (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 6.4.1).

n.0: The CPO represents users, but the book recommends writing personas together in a cross-functional workshop, not by one role from research (book 6.4.1).
n.1: Project support assists with stakeholder analysis, but personas are created in a cross-functional workshop with the development team (book 6.4.1, Table 7.2).
n.2: The mandate triggers starting up; personas are defined collaboratively later, for example in the project initiation workshop (book 6.4.1, Table 13.7).

Agile: Practices & Business Case.q:
Identify the missing word in the following sentence.
PRINCE2 Agile recommends that personas are written in a cross-functional workshop and kept [?], because the abstraction leaves more room for innovation.
o: fictional
demographic
individual
permanent
Agile: Practices & Business Case.w: Personas should be fictional: the abstraction from real people widens the room for innovative solutions (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 6.4.1).

n.1: Personas are based on user needs, not demographics such as age, occupation or income (book 6.4.1).
n.2: Describing real individuals removes the abstraction that the book says supports innovation (book 6.4.1).
n.3: Personas are refined as understanding of users grows; the book's point here is that they are fictional (book 6.4.1).

Agile: Practices & Business Case.q: What is the recommended maximum number of personas for an agile pilot project or a new product?
o: Three
Seven
Five
Ten
Agile: Practices & Business Case.w: More than five personas is not recommended for agile pilots or new products; a larger set is possible only when agile maturity is high (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 6.4.1).

n.0: Three echoes the one to three key user groups prioritized in the project canvas workshop; the persona limit is five (book Table 13.2, 6.4.1).
n.1: Seven is above the recommended maximum of five for pilots and new products (book 6.4.1).
n.3: Ten is well above the recommended maximum of five for pilots and new products (book 6.4.1).

Agile: Practices & Business Case.q: A team is writing personas for a new mobile banking service. On what does PRINCE2 Agile recommend the personas are based?
o: Age, occupation and income data about the users
The job titles of the sponsoring managers
The defects recorded in the issue register
The needs that the users have in common
Agile: Practices & Business Case.w: Demographics such as age, occupation and income no longer predict what users share, so personas are based on user needs (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 6.4.1).

n.0: Age, occupation and income are demographics, which the book says no longer predict shared needs (book 6.4.1).
n.1: Sponsoring managers are stakeholders, not the users the personas represent; personas are based on user needs (book 6.4.1).
n.2: The issue register records issues raised during the project; personas start from user needs (book Table 11.1, 6.4.1).

Agile: Practices & Business Case.q: The team for a new product has drafted nine personas. Why does PRINCE2 Agile advise against having this many?
o: Each persona above five must be approved by the project board as a baseline change to the canvas
Too many user needs shift focus from key users, make prioritizing harder and take too long to meet
Each persona needs its own product owner and delivery team, which adds to the cost of the project
Story points cannot be estimated reliably once a project has more than five personas to satisfy
Agile: Practices & Business Case.w: Above five personas, for pilots and new products, focus moves away from key users, prioritizing requirements becomes harder and meeting all the needs takes too long for the deadlines (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 6.4.1).

n.0: The book gives no board approval rule for personas; the concern is loss of focus, harder prioritization and time (book 6.4.1).
n.2: Personas describe users, not teams; delivery teams are organized around products and backlogs (book 6.4.1, 7.3.1).
n.3: Estimation is relative sizing of stories by the team; the persona limit is about focus and prioritization (book 8.4.3, 6.4.1).

Agile: Practices & Business Case.q: In which agile workshop is persona definition one of the topics?
o: Project canvas workshop
Project kickoff workshop
Project initiation workshop
Release planning workshop
Agile: Practices & Business Case.w: Persona definition, identifying and defining key user personas, is a topic of the project initiation workshop in initiating a project (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.7).

n.0: The project canvas workshop includes user group definition (one to three key groups), but persona definition is a project initiation workshop topic (book Table 13.2, Table 13.7).
n.1: The kickoff workshop covers team topics such as psychological safety, values and norms, the skill matrix and dashboards (book Table 13.8).
n.3: The release planning workshop, at a stage boundary, covers introduction, OKR definition, release planning and wrap-up (book Table 13.16).

Agile: Practices & Business Case.q: In which situation can a PRINCE2 Agile project reasonably use a set of more than five personas?
o: When the organization's agile maturity is high
When the project has more than five delivery teams
When the project is a pilot of agile ways of working
When the users come from many demographic groups
Agile: Practices & Business Case.w: The persona set can be enlarged when agile maturity is high; above five is not recommended for agile pilots or new products (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 6.4.1).

n.1: The number of teams is not the criterion; the book links a larger persona set to high agile maturity (book 6.4.1).
n.2: Pilots are exactly where more than five personas is not recommended (book 6.4.1).
n.3: Personas are based on needs, not demographics, so demographic variety does not justify more personas (book 6.4.1).

Agile: Practices & Business Case.q: Which PRINCE2 Agile practice provides the mechanisms for judging whether a project is, and remains, desirable, viable and achievable, as a basis for decisions about continued investment?
o: Business case
Progress
Organization
Risk
Agile: Practices & Business Case.w: The business case practice exists to establish mechanisms for judging whether the project is (and stays) desirable, viable and achievable, which supports decisions on continued investment (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 6.1).

n.1: Progress monitors actual achievement against plan and forecasts continued viability, but judging desirability, viability and achievability for investment decisions is the business case purpose (book 12.1, 6.1).
n.2: Organization establishes the structure of accountability and responsibilities; it decides who takes investment decisions, not whether the investment is justified (book 7.1).
n.3: Risk identifies, assesses and controls uncertainty that could affect objectives; it does not provide the overall judgement of desirability, viability and achievability (book 10.1).

Agile: Practices & Business Case.q: What is the purpose of the organization practice in a PRINCE2 Agile project?
o: To collect and assess issues and to control changes to the project's baseline
To define and establish the project's structure of accountability and responsibilities
To define the products to be delivered and the means by which they will be delivered
To monitor and compare actual achievements against those planned
Agile: Practices & Business Case.w: The organization practice defines and establishes the project's structure of accountability and responsibilities, in other words who does what (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 7.1).

n.0: Collecting and assessing issues and controlling baseline changes is the purpose of the issues practice (book 11.1).
n.2: Defining the products and the means of delivering them is the purpose of the plans practice (book 8.1).
n.3: Monitoring and comparing actual against planned achievement is part of the purpose of the progress practice (book 12.1).

Agile: Practices & Business Case.q: Which practice exists to document the users' requirements of the project products and to establish the means by which those requirements will be met?
o: Plans
Business case
Quality
Issues
Agile: Practices & Business Case.w: The quality practice documents users' requirements of the project products and establishes how they will be met, answering what is acceptable to users and how it can be measured (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 9.1, Table 5.2).

n.0: Plans define the products to be delivered and the who, how, where, when and how much of delivering them; users' quality requirements belong to the quality practice (book 8.1).
n.1: The business case judges whether the project is desirable, viable and achievable; it does not document users' requirements of the products (book 6.1).
n.3: Issues collects and assesses issues and controls changes to the baseline; it does not set out the users' requirements in the first place (book 11.1).

Agile: Practices & Business Case.q:
Identify the missing word in the following sentence.
The purpose of the [?] practice includes establishing mechanisms to compare actual achievements against those planned, providing a forecast for the project objectives and its continued viability, and controlling any deviations that would cause an exception.
o: business case
issues
plans
progress
Agile: Practices & Business Case.w: Monitoring actual against planned achievement, forecasting objectives and continued viability, and controlling deviations that cause an exception together form the purpose of the progress practice (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 12.1).

n.0: Business case judges whether the project is desirable, viable and achievable; comparing actual with planned achievement and controlling deviations that cause an exception is the progress purpose (book 6.1, 12.1).
n.1: Issues controls changes to the project's baseline; controlling deviations that cause an exception is the progress purpose (book 11.1, 12.1).
n.2: Plans define the products and the means of delivering them; comparing achievement with those plans is done through the progress practice (book 8.1, 12.1).

Agile: Organization & Roles.q: A PRINCE2 Agile project is growing from one delivery team to four teams working in parallel. Which statement about the project management team structure is correct?
o: Each delivery team needs its own project manager to agree its work packages
There is one project manager, and there may be a product owner for each team
The team coaches are merged into one agile coach role that covers every team
Each delivery team uses a smaller composition than a single-team project would
Agile: Organization & Roles.w: With multiple teams (book Figure 7.2) there is still one project manager, while there can be several product owners. Team composition stays the same as in a single-team project, and team coaches and the agile coach remain separate roles.

n.0: Scaling adds teams and product owners, not project managers: one PM runs the project for the board.
n.2: The team coach and agile coach are different roles; a team coach works with one or two teams, the agile coach at organization level.
n.3: Each team in a multi-team project has the same composition as the team in a single-team project.

Agile: Organization & Roles.q: In PRINCE2 Agile the project manager is expected to act as a servant leader. What does this mean for the way the project manager works?
o: They facilitate collaboration between the governance roles and the delivery teams
They allocate individual tasks to each developer and tester at the daily stand-up
They take ownership of each delivery team's product backlog and its priorities
They replace the project board as the point of accountability for the project
Agile: Organization & Roles.w: The project manager runs the project day to day within tolerances and acts as a servant leader who links governance and the teams, facilitating collaboration between them (book Table 7.2, Table B.1).

n.1: Delivery teams self-manage under their product owner; a servant-leader PM does not hand out individual tasks.
n.2: Each team's product backlog is owned by its product owner, and priorities across teams are set by the CPO.
n.3: Accountability for the project stays with the project executive and the board; the PM manages on their behalf.

Agile: Organization & Roles.q:
Which two statements about the organization practice in a PRINCE2 Agile project are correct?
1. The chief product owner sets priorities across the delivery teams.
2. The agile coach holds line authority over each delivery team.
3. The project manager owns the product backlog of each team.
4. The product owner is a version of the team manager role.
o: 1 and 2
2 and 3
3 and 4
1 and 4
Agile: Organization & Roles.w: Statement 1 is correct: the CPO owns the project backlog and sets priorities across teams. Statement 4 is correct: the PO is a version of the team manager role (book 7.3.1, Table 7.2).

n.0: Statement 2 is wrong: the agile coach advises and mentors at organization level and holds no line authority over teams.
n.1: Both are wrong: the agile coach has no line authority over teams, and each product backlog is owned by its product owner, not the PM.
n.2: Statement 3 is wrong: the product owner, not the project manager, owns the team's product backlog.

Agile: Organization & Roles.q: A senior manager worries that self-managing delivery teams will weaken project governance. How does PRINCE2 Agile combine self-management with governance?
o: Teams manage themselves freely, and the board reviews what they built at closure
Teams follow detailed task instructions that the project manager issues each day
Teams self-manage within tolerances and constraints agreed with the project manager
Teams report straight to the project executive, who sets their daily priorities
Agile: Organization & Roles.w: Product owners deliver the allocated work within the tolerances and constraints agreed with the project manager, and the team coach helps the team balance self-management with the principles and tolerances (book Table 7.2, Table B.1). Self-management sits inside governance.

n.0: PRINCE2 Agile keeps control during delivery through tolerances, work packages and dashboards, not just a review at closure.
n.1: Issuing daily task instructions would remove the self-management that PRINCE2 Agile teams are given.
n.3: Teams work through their product owner and the project manager; the executive is accountable at board level and does not set daily priorities.

Agile: Organization & Roles.q: A PRINCE2 Agile project needs one role to represent the user community, own the project backlog and keep it refined with input from users. Which role is this?
o: The product owner of the lead delivery team
The project executive on the project board
The chief product owner
The senior supplier on the project board
Agile: Organization & Roles.w: The chief product owner represents the user community, owns the project backlog and keeps it refined with user input and aligned with the teams' product backlogs (book Table 7.2, Table B.1).

n.0: A product owner owns one team's product backlog, not the project backlog, and does not represent the whole user community.
n.1: The project executive is accountable for the project and its strategic alignment; the CPO represents the users.
n.3: The senior supplier represents the supplier side, those who design and build the products, not the users.

Agile: Organization & Roles.q: Which of the following is a responsibility of the project executive in a PRINCE2 Agile project?
o: Keeping each team's product backlog aligned with the project backlog
Monitoring adherence to the PRINCE2 Agile principles and agile practices
Removing systemic blockers to agile adoption across the organization
Approving the tolerances within which agile decision-making takes place
Agile: Organization & Roles.w: The project executive is accountable for the project and approves the tolerances for agile decision-making, as well as the project brief, management approaches and team structure (book Table B.1).

n.0: Keeping a team's product backlog aligned with the project backlog is the product owner's responsibility.
n.1: Monitoring adherence to principles and agile practices is the role of project assurance.
n.2: Removing organization-wide blockers to agile adoption is the agile coach's responsibility.

Agile: Organization & Roles.q: A project board wants independent feedback on whether the delivery teams are balancing agility with control. Which statement describes the role that provides this in PRINCE2 Agile?
o: Project assurance monitors adherence to agile practices and governance checks
Project support gives administrative help with iterations, workshops and data
The chief product owner sets priorities so that user requirements are met
The agile coach mentors the organization and removes blockers across teams
Agile: Organization & Roles.w: Project assurance monitors adherence to the PRINCE2 Agile principles and agile practices, builds quality and governance checks into iterative delivery and gives feedback on balancing agility with control (book Table 7.2, Table B.1).

n.1: Project support is administrative support and tools advice; it does not provide independent assurance to the board.
n.2: The CPO represents users and sets priorities; independent monitoring of governance is not part of that role.
n.3: The agile coach helps the organization adopt agile; independent monitoring for the board is the role of project assurance.

Agile: Organization & Roles.q: Which governance-level role in a PRINCE2 Agile project represents the interests of those who design, develop and deliver the project's products?
o: The chief product owner
The senior supplier
The project executive
Project assurance
Agile: Organization & Roles.w: The senior supplier represents the supplier interest: the people who design, develop and deliver the products (book Table 7.2; consistent with the PRINCE2 7 supplier interest represented by the senior supplier).

n.0: The chief product owner represents the user community, not the suppliers.
n.2: The project executive represents the business interest and is accountable for the project.
n.3: Project assurance monitors and advises; it does not represent a stakeholder interest on the board.

Agile: Organization & Roles.q: Three delivery teams are each building screens for a new customer portal, and users complain that the teams style their screens differently. Which role is responsible for setting a consistent priority on branding across all three teams?
o: The product owner of each delivery team
The project manager
The agile coach
The chief product owner
Agile: Organization & Roles.w: The CPO sets priorities across the delivery teams, for example making sure branding is consistent across every team's products, and ensures user requirements are met (book Table 7.2, Table B.1).

n.0: Each product owner manages one team's product backlog; priorities that cut across teams belong to the CPO.
n.1: The project manager runs the project day to day but does not prioritize the product content across teams.
n.2: The agile coach supports agile adoption at organization level; prioritizing user requirements is not part of the role.

Agile: Organization & Roles.q:
Identify the missing words in the following sentence.
In PRINCE2 Agile, the [?] keeps the project backlog refined with input from users and aligned with the product backlogs of the delivery teams.
o: product owner of each team
project manager
chief product owner
project support
Agile: Organization & Roles.w: The chief product owner owns the project backlog, keeps it refined with user input and aligns it with the delivery-level product backlogs (book Table B.1).

n.0: Each team's product owner keeps their own product backlog aligned with the project backlog; the project backlog itself is the CPO's.
n.1: The project manager consults on backlogs but does not own or refine the project backlog.
n.3: Project support helps with administration and dashboards; it does not own any backlog.

Agile: Organization & Roles.q: Which role in a PRINCE2 Agile project is accountable for the project and approves the project brief, the management approaches and the project management team structure?
o: The chief product owner
The project executive
The project manager
Project assurance
Agile: Organization & Roles.w: The project executive is accountable for the project and approves the project brief, the management approaches and the project management team structure (book Table B.1).

n.0: The CPO represents users and owns the project backlog; approval of these products rests with the executive.
n.2: The project manager prepares these products but does not approve them.
n.3: Project assurance may advise on these products but does not approve them.

Agile: Organization & Roles.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes the project executive from the chief product owner (CPO) in PRINCE2 Agile?
o: The executive is accountable for the project; the CPO represents users and sets priorities
The executive owns the project backlog; the CPO approves tolerances for agile decisions
The executive sets priorities across the teams; the CPO owns the business justification
The executive manages day to day; the CPO gives independent assurance to the board
Agile: Organization & Roles.w: The executive is accountable for the project and approves tolerances for agile decision-making; the CPO represents the user community, owns the project backlog and sets priorities across teams (book Table 7.2, Table B.1).

n.1: The responsibilities are reversed: the CPO owns the project backlog and the executive approves the tolerances.
n.2: Setting priorities across teams is the CPO's job, and business justification sits with the executive.
n.3: Day-to-day management is the PM's job and independent assurance belongs to project assurance.

Agile: Organization & Roles.q: Before each progress review, someone on a PRINCE2 Agile project updates the project and team dashboards and pulls information from them to meet reporting needs. Which role normally does this?
o: Project assurance
Project support
The team coach
The chief product owner
Agile: Organization & Roles.w: Project support provides administrative support tailored to iterations and workshops, including updating and pulling information from the project and team dashboards to meet reporting needs (book Table 7.2, Table B.1).

n.0: Project assurance monitors adherence and advises the board and PM; maintaining dashboards is an administrative support task.
n.2: The team coach supports a team's self-management and workshops; reporting from dashboards is done by project support.
n.3: The CPO represents users and owns the project backlog; dashboard administration is not part of that role.

Agile: Organization & Roles.q: Which statement describes the agile coach role in PRINCE2 Agile?
o: A mentor who helps the organization adopt agile and removes blockers across teams
A facilitator who works inside one or two teams to help them manage themselves
An independent reviewer who checks that governance controls are being followed
A team-level leader who owns a delivery team's backlog and its user stories
Agile: Organization & Roles.w: The agile coach mentors and facilitates the organization in adopting and sustaining agile, works across teams to remove systemic blockers and supports the board, project assurance and the PM with expert agile knowledge (book Table 7.2, Table B.1).

n.1: Working closely with one or two specific teams on self-management describes the team coach, not the agile coach.
n.2: Independent checking of governance and agile practices is the role of project assurance.
n.3: Owning a delivery team's product backlog and user stories describes the product owner.

Agile: Organization & Roles.q: Which statement describes the authority of the project manager in a PRINCE2 Agile project?
o: They set priorities across all delivery teams on behalf of the users
They approve the tolerances for agile decision-making on the project
They direct the daily work of each developer and tester in the teams
They run the project day to day for the board within agreed tolerances
Agile: Organization & Roles.w: The project manager has authority to run the project on a day-to-day basis on behalf of the board, within the tolerances and constraints the board has agreed (book Table 7.2, Table B.1).

n.0: Setting priorities across teams on behalf of users is the chief product owner's responsibility.
n.1: Approving tolerances for agile decision-making is the project executive's responsibility.
n.2: Delivery team members are led by their product owner and manage their own work; the PM does not direct them individually.

Agile: Organization & Roles.q: Senior managers in a company's finance function insist that every delivery team completes detailed weekly timesheets by task, which is undermining self-management in several teams. Which PRINCE2 Agile role is BEST placed to help remove this blocker?
o: The team coach of the team most affected
Project support
The agile coach
The product owner of each team
Agile: Organization & Roles.w: The agile coach works across teams and at organization level to identify and remove systemic blockers to agile adoption, supporting the board and PM with expert agile knowledge (book Table 7.2, Table B.1). An organization-wide practice affecting several teams is such a blocker.

n.0: A team coach works within one or two teams; a blocker rooted in another part of the organization and affecting several teams calls for the agile coach.
n.1: Project support provides administrative help and facilitates communication; tackling organization-level obstacles to agile is the agile coach's role.
n.3: Product owners lead their own teams' backlogs; they are not positioned to change an organization-wide practice.

Agile: Organization & Roles.q: Which of the following is a responsibility of project support in a PRINCE2 Agile project?
o: Helping with stakeholder analysis and communication between board and teams
Advising the board on how an exception report affects the project canvas
Helping a delivery team to write user stories and run its team workshops
Mentoring the project manager and the board on agile leadership and adoption
Agile: Organization & Roles.w: Project support assists with stakeholder analysis and documentation, compiles lists and facilitates communication between governance roles and teams, alongside administrative and tools support (book Table 7.2, Table B.1).

n.1: Advising the board and PM on exception reports and impacts on the project canvas is a project assurance responsibility.
n.2: Helping a team write user stories and facilitating team workshops is the team coach's role.
n.3: Mentoring leadership in agile adoption is the agile coach's role.

Agile: Organization & Roles.q:
Which two statements about the agile coach and the team coach in PRINCE2 Agile are correct?
1. The agile coach facilitates each team's retrospectives as its main duty.
2. The agile coach works across teams on organization-level obstacles to agile.
3. The team coach advises the project board on agile governance.
4. The team coach usually works closely with one or two specific teams.
o: 1 and 2
1 and 3
3 and 4
2 and 4
Agile: Organization & Roles.w: Statement 2 is correct: the agile coach works across teams to remove systemic blockers. Statement 4 is correct: the team coach works closely with one or two specific teams (book Table 7.2, Table B.1).

n.0: Statement 1 is wrong: facilitating team workshops such as retrospectives is a team coach activity, not the agile coach's main duty.
n.1: Both are wrong: team workshops belong to the team coach, and supporting the board with agile knowledge belongs to the agile coach.
n.2: Statement 3 is wrong: supporting the board, assurance and PM with expert agile knowledge is the agile coach's role.

Agile: Organization & Roles.q: In a PRINCE2 Agile project, the project manager is preparing the product backlogs and the management approaches. Who should the project manager consult?
o: The agile coach, who approves the management approaches
Project support, who owns the team product backlogs
The product owners and the relevant stakeholders
The developers, who set the priorities for each team
Agile: Organization & Roles.w: The project manager consults the product owners and stakeholders when preparing product backlogs and management approaches (book Table B.1).

n.0: The agile coach advises on agile ways of working, but the management approaches are approved by the project executive.
n.1: Product backlogs are owned by the product owners; project support provides administrative help.
n.3: Developers build the increments; priorities come from the product owner within the team and the CPO across teams.

Agile: Organization & Roles.q: Which of these responsibilities belongs to the project manager rather than to the chief product owner in a PRINCE2 Agile project?
o: Keeping the project backlog refined with regular input from users
Ensuring that project risks are identified, assessed and controlled
Setting priorities across the backlogs of all the delivery teams
Making sure that the products meet the user community's requirements
Agile: Organization & Roles.w: The project manager runs the project day to day and ensures risks are identified, assessed and controlled (book Table B.1). The other three are CPO responsibilities.

n.0: Refining the project backlog with user input is a CPO responsibility.
n.2: Prioritizing across teams belongs to the CPO; the PM does not prioritize across teams.
n.3: Ensuring user requirements are met is the CPO's responsibility, not the PM's.

Agile: Organization & Roles.q: A delivery team in a PRINCE2 Agile project keeps its user stories in a product backlog. Which role owns this team's product backlog?
o: The chief product owner
The project manager
The team coach
The product owner
Agile: Organization & Roles.w: The product owner owns the team's product backlog and keeps it aligned with the project backlog, continued business justification and tolerances (book Table 7.2, Table B.1).

n.0: The CPO owns the project backlog and sets priorities across teams, not each team's product backlog.
n.1: The project manager consults on product backlogs but does not own them.
n.2: The team coach helps the team write user stories but does not own the backlog.

Agile: Organization & Roles.q: An organization moving to PRINCE2 Agile has an experienced Scrum master who will support one delivery team. Which PRINCE2 Agile role does a Scrum master fit?
o: Product owner
Agile coach
Team coach
Project manager
Agile: Organization & Roles.w: A Scrum master fits the team coach role, which works closely with one or two teams to help them self-manage, refine processes and run team workshops (book Table 7.2, Table B.1).

n.0: The product owner owns the team's product backlog; that matches the Scrum product owner, not the Scrum master.
n.1: The agile coach works at organization level across teams, whereas a Scrum master supports a team.
n.3: The project manager runs the project for the board; Scrum has no equivalent of this role.

Agile: Organization & Roles.q: Which responsibility belongs to the tester role in a PRINCE2 Agile delivery team?
o: Designing, building and maintaining the increments of the team's product
Reviewing products against acceptance criteria and the team Definition of Done
Preparing user stories and keeping the product backlog aligned to the project
Helping the team to self-manage, refine its processes and resolve conflicts
Agile: Organization & Roles.w: The tester designs, runs and possibly automates tests and quality reviews and reviews products against acceptance or quality criteria and the team Definition of Done (book Table 7.2, Table B.1).

n.0: Designing, building and maintaining increments is the developer's responsibility.
n.2: Preparing user stories and aligning the product backlog is the product owner's responsibility.
n.3: Supporting self-management, process refinement and conflict resolution is the team coach's role.

Agile: Organization & Roles.q: Which statement describes the developer role in PRINCE2 Agile?
o: Designs, develops and maintains product increments and resolves technical issues
Designs and runs tests, then checks products against the team Definition of Done
Facilitates the team's workshops and helps the team to write its user stories
Agrees the work package descriptions for the team with the project manager
Agile: Organization & Roles.w: The developer designs, develops and maintains increments of the products, resolves technical issues and keeps improving the outputs (book Table 7.2, Table B.1).

n.1: Designing and running tests against the team DoD describes the tester.
n.2: Facilitating team workshops and helping write user stories describes the team coach.
n.3: Agreeing work package descriptions with the PM is a product owner responsibility.

Agile: Organization & Roles.q: A product owner in a PRINCE2 Agile project is refining the team's product backlog. What must the product owner keep the product backlog aligned with?
o: The team skill matrix and the team delegation matrix
The commercial management approach and supplier contracts
The project backlog, business justification and tolerances
The senior supplier's technical standards and resource plans
Agile: Organization & Roles.w: The PO owns the product backlog and keeps it aligned with the project backlog, the continued business justification principle and the project tolerances (book Table B.1).

n.0: The skill and delegation matrices support team working; they are not what the product backlog must align with.
n.1: The commercial management approach covers procurement and contracts, not the content of a team's product backlog.
n.3: Supplier standards may inform quality, but the PO's backlog alignment is with the project backlog, justification and tolerances.

Agile: Organization & Roles.q: Which of the following is a responsibility of the team coach in PRINCE2 Agile?
o: Setting the priority of user stories across all the delivery teams
Helping the team balance self-management with the agreed tolerances
Agreeing work package descriptions for the team with the project manager
Removing obstacles to agile adoption across the wider organization
Agile: Organization & Roles.w: The team coach helps the team self-manage while balancing that with the PRINCE2 Agile principles and tolerances; it also facilitates team workshops and helps with user stories (book Table B.1).

n.0: Prioritizing across teams is the chief product owner's responsibility.
n.2: Agreeing work package descriptions with the PM is the product owner's responsibility.
n.3: Removing organization-wide obstacles is the agile coach's responsibility.

Agile: Organization & Roles.q:
Identify the missing words in the following sentence.
In PRINCE2 Agile, the [?] is a version of the team manager role and delivers the allocated work within the tolerances agreed with the project manager.
o: product owner
team coach
chief product owner
senior supplier
Agile: Organization & Roles.w: The product owner is a version of the team manager role and delivers allocated work within tolerances agreed with the PM (book 7.3.1, Table 7.2).

n.1: The team coach supports a team's self-management; it is not the team manager equivalent and holds no work packages.
n.2: The CPO is a governance-level role representing users across teams, not a team manager version.
n.3: The senior supplier is a governance-level role representing suppliers, not the team-level manager.

Agile: Organization & Roles.q: A delivery team includes an analyst whose main task is to check each released feature against its acceptance criteria and measure whether it has the expected impact. Which PRINCE2 Agile role does this person fit BEST?
o: Developer
Product owner
Team coach
Tester
Agile: Organization & Roles.w: Checking products against acceptance or quality criteria and measuring their impact is quality work, which fits the tester role better than the developer role (book Table 7.2, Table B.1).

n.0: Developers design, build and maintain increments; checking against acceptance criteria fits the tester.
n.1: The product owner owns the backlog and agrees work with the PM; checking released features is a tester activity.
n.2: The team coach supports team self-management and workshops, not quality checking of products.

Agile: Organization & Roles.q: What is the purpose of the commercial management approach in a PRINCE2 Agile project?
o: To make sure procurement and the form of contract support agile product development
To define who is in the project management team and how its members work together
To describe each project role and the specific responsibilities that it carries
To record the skills, strengths and gaps of each member of a delivery team
Agile: Organization & Roles.w: In PRINCE2 Agile the commercial management approach makes sure the form of procurement and contract supports agile product development, for example fixed teams and costs per iteration, a defined MVP and tolerances, and an agreed Definition of Done (book 7.3.2, Table 7.3).

n.1: Who is involved and how they work together is the purpose of the project management team structure.
n.2: Describing roles and their specific responsibilities is the purpose of the role descriptions.
n.3: Recording skills, strengths and gaps is done with the team skill matrix, an organization technique rather than this product.

Agile: Organization & Roles.q: A PRINCE2 Agile project has teams in two cities. The project manager wants to document how the remote teams will work together, including the tools they will use for transparency and rich communication. In which product should this be described?
o: Role descriptions
Project management team structure
Commercial management approach
Team delegation matrix
Agile: Organization & Roles.w: The project management team structure sets out who is involved, how they relate and how they work together, including arrangements for co-located or remote teams and the tools used for transparency and rich communication (book 7.3.2, Table 7.3).

n.0: Role descriptions set out each role's specific responsibilities, not team working arrangements across locations.
n.2: The commercial management approach covers procurement and contracts, not how remote teams collaborate.
n.3: A delegation matrix shows who decides and who is involved per decision area; working arrangements and tools for remote teams belong in the team structure.

Agile: Organization & Roles.q: A project manager wants to set out, for each role used on a PRINCE2 Agile project, the specific responsibilities that the person filling it will carry. Which product should be used?
o: Commercial management approach
Team delegation matrix
Role descriptions
Team skill matrix
Agile: Organization & Roles.w: Role descriptions record the roles in the project management team and their specific responsibilities, such as a note that the PM will be mentored by the agile coach (book 7.3.2, Table 7.3).

n.0: The commercial management approach covers procurement and contracting, not the responsibilities of each project role.
n.1: A delegation matrix shows who decides and who is involved per decision area; it does not describe each role's full responsibilities.
