The purpose of the [?] process is to provide a fixed point at which acceptance of the project product is confirmed.
o: managing a stage boundary
directing a project
controlling a stage
closing a project
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: Closing a project provides a fixed point at which acceptance of the project product is confirmed and the achievement of objectives recognized (PRINCE2 7 manual 19.1; PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.18 'confirm project acceptance').

n.0: Managing a stage boundary prepares information for the board's review of a stage and the next stage plan; it is not the final acceptance point (book 13.7.1).
n.1: Directing a project includes the board authorizing closure, but the process whose purpose is the fixed point for confirming acceptance is closing a project (book 13.3.1).
n.2: Controlling a stage keeps the work of a stage within tolerances; it does not provide the project's acceptance point (book 13.5.1).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: Near the end of a stage, the board of a hospital trust's scheduling project wants to review how the stage went, see the updated release map for the next stage, and confirm that the business justification and risks are still acceptable. Which process has the purpose of providing the board with this information?
o: Controlling a stage
Managing a stage boundary
Directing a project
Managing product delivery
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: Managing a stage boundary gives the board enough information to review the success of the current stage, review the updated release map, approve the next stage plan and confirm continued business justification and acceptability of the risks (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 13.7.1).

n.0: Controlling a stage keeps the current stage on track and reports progress; preparing the information for the stage-end review is managing a stage boundary (book 13.5.1, 13.7.1).
n.2: Directing a project is where the board makes the decision, but the process whose purpose is to supply the information for that decision is managing a stage boundary (book 13.3.1, 13.7.1).
n.3: Managing product delivery controls the link between the project manager and the delivery team for work packages; it does not prepare the board's stage-end review (book 13.6.1).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: A county council's project mandate for a library booking system has just been received. In the 'starting up a project' process, which role leads the development of the project canvas from the mandate?
o: The project manager
The chief product owner
The project executive
Project support
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: When preparing the outline business case in starting up, the project executive leads the development of the project canvas from the mandate (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.1).

n.0: The project manager works with the CPO, senior supplier and executive to define what will be delivered and create the project backlog, but the executive leads the canvas (book Table 13.1).
n.1: The CPO helps define what is to be delivered and the project backlog; leading the project canvas from the mandate is the executive's task (book Table 13.1).
n.3: Project support gives administrative help, such as keeping dashboards up to date; it does not lead the project canvas (book Table B.1).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: Which workshop in the 'starting up a project' process aims to create a shared understanding and a clear foundation by defining the project's core elements in line with the organization's goals?
o: The project canvas workshop
The starting up workshop
The project initiation workshop
The project kickoff workshop
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: The project canvas workshop builds shared understanding and a clear foundation by defining the core elements of the project in line with organizational goals (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 13.2.4.1, Table 13.2).

n.1: The starting up workshop also supports starting up, but its topics are project roles, lessons review, initiation stage planning, risk analysis and refine planning (book Table 13.3).
n.2: The project initiation workshop supports initiating a project, aligning on vision and objectives, the release map and management approaches (book 13.4.4.1).
n.3: The project kickoff workshop supports initiating a project, building teamwork and an agile culture of openness and self-management (book 13.4.4.2).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: In the starting up workshop for a retail chain's stock-control project, participants split into small groups to collect lessons from earlier initiatives and discuss their impact. Which topic of the starting up workshop is this?
o: Project roles
Refine planning
Risk analysis
Lessons review
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: In the lessons review topic, small groups gather lessons from previous initiatives and consider their impact (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.3).

n.0: The project roles topic aligns participants on the team and the role descriptions, not on lessons from earlier work (book Table 13.3).
n.1: Refine planning updates the initiation stage plan and related documents, including the release map, after the other topics (book Table 13.3).
n.2: Risk analysis looks at threats and opportunities that could affect initiation or the project, not at lessons from previous initiatives (book Table 13.3).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: A project manager has just been appointed to a water company's metering project and is about to begin the 'starting up a project' process. At which point in this process does the project manager create the daily log?
o: When lessons from previous similar projects are assessed
When the project executive and the project manager are appointed
When the project brief is assembled for the board's approval
When the initiation stage and its release map are planned
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: The project manager creates the daily log in the 'appoint the project executive and the project manager' activity, at the very start of the process (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.1).

n.0: In 'assess previous lessons' the project manager reviews lessons from similar projects and may create the lessons log; the daily log already exists (book Table 13.1).
n.2: Assembling the project brief confirms objectives, scope, tolerances, constraints, assumptions and dependencies; it does not create the daily log (book Table 13.1).
n.3: Planning the initiation stage sets time and cost constraints, a high-level release map for initiation and controls; the daily log is created earlier (book Table 13.1).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: In a project canvas workshop for a new parcel-tracking service, participants agree one to three key user groups and put them in priority order. Which topic of the project canvas workshop is being covered?
o: User group definition
Persona definition
Business option selection
Scope definition
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: User group definition identifies one to three key user groups and prioritizes them (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.2).

n.1: Persona definition is a topic of the project initiation workshop in initiating a project, not of the project canvas workshop (book Table 13.7).
n.2: Business option selection chooses between the possible business options for the project; it does not identify and rank user groups (book Table 13.2).
n.3: Scope definition sets the timeline, tolerances and scope as prioritized epics; it is not about choosing key user groups (book Table 13.2).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: A project manager in starting up needs the project canvas workshop and the starting up workshop to take place. According to PRINCE2 Agile, who defines the participants for these workshops, sets the dates and invites everyone?
o: The project executive
The chief product owner
The project manager
The agile coach
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: In starting up a project, the project manager defines the participants for the project canvas workshop and the starting up workshop, sets the dates and invites all participants (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 13.2.3).

n.0: The project executive leads the project canvas content, but organizing these workshops is the project manager's task (book 13.2.3, Table 13.1).
n.1: The CPO takes part in defining what is to be delivered, but arranging the starting up workshops is the project manager's task (book 13.2.3).
n.3: The agile coach supports agile adoption across the organization; the book gives the arrangement of these workshops to the project manager (book 13.2.3).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: In the 'starting up a project' process, the project manager confirms the objectives, scope, exclusions, tolerances, constraints, assumptions and the dependencies on other initiatives. Which activity is this?
o: Prepare the outline business case
Assemble the project brief
Select the project approach
Plan the initiation stage
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: Assembling the project brief confirms objectives, outcomes, scope, exclusions, tolerances, constraints, assumptions and dependencies, for example on other initiatives (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.1).

n.0: Preparing the outline business case is where the executive leads the project canvas and the project backlog is created (book Table 13.1).
n.2: Selecting the project approach evaluates delivery solutions, decides the approach and defines tailoring needs where known (book Table 13.1).
n.3: Planning the initiation stage sets time and cost constraints for initiation, a high-level release map for initiation and its controls (book Table 13.1).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: In the project canvas workshop, how is the project's scope typically expressed under the scope definition topic?
o: As a team plan of user stories selected for the first iteration
As team OKRs agreed with each delivery team for the first release
As the project Definition of Ready and Definition of Done criteria
As epics prioritized using MoSCoW, with a timeline and tolerances
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: Under scope definition, the canvas sets the timeline and tolerances and expresses scope as epics prioritized with MoSCoW, with targets, collaborations and dependencies (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.2).

n.0: Selecting user stories into a team plan happens in the team planning workshop of managing product delivery (book Table 13.13).
n.1: Team OKRs are defined or updated in the release planning workshop at a stage boundary (book Table 13.16).
n.2: The project Definition of Ready and Definition of Done are topics of the project initiation workshop in initiating a project (book Table 13.7).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: An insurer's project board wants agile maturity and the risks of agile working on its claims project to be assessed regularly during initiation and later stages. Which named workshop supports the 'directing a project' process for this?
o: The progress review workshop
The project initiation workshop
The release planning workshop
The agile enablement workshop
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: To assess agile maturity and agile risks regularly, Agilometer assessments are carried out in initiation and later stages in a workshop for the board, agile coaches and organizational or business representatives: the agile enablement workshop (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 13.3.3).

n.0: The progress review workshop supports controlling a stage, reviewing project dashboard metrics, risks and issues and demonstrating completed features (book 13.5.4.1).
n.1: The project initiation workshop is where the Agilometer is first assessed by all participants in initiating a project; the regular board-level reviews take place in the agile enablement workshop (book Table 13.7, 13.3.3).
n.2: The release planning workshop supports managing a stage boundary, defining team OKRs and updating the release map (book 13.7.4.1).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: A project manager is setting up the agile enablement workshop for a university's student records project. Which group of participants is this workshop intended for?
o: The delivery team, its product owner and its team coach for the coming iteration
The project board, agile coaches and organizational or business representatives
The project manager, project support and the developers working in each team
The chief product owner, the developers and the users who will accept the product
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: The agile enablement workshop is a special workshop for the project board, agile coaches and organizational or business representatives, held to review agile maturity and agile risks (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 13.3.3, Table 13.5).

n.0: A delivery team with its product owner and team coach describes the team planning or team retrospective workshops in managing product delivery (book 13.6.4).
n.2: The project manager, project support and developers are not the audience the book gives; the enablement workshop centres on the board with agile coaches and business representatives (book 13.3.3).
n.3: The CPO, developers and accepting users fit a product demo; the enablement workshop is a board-level session on agile maturity and risk (book 13.3.3).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: In the 'directing a project' process, the board of a logistics firm approves the project brief and the release map for initiation, and then authorizes the project manager to begin initiation. Which board activity is this?
o: Authorize the project
Authorize a stage or exception plan
Authorize initiation
Give ongoing direction
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: In 'authorize initiation' the board approves the project brief and the release map for initiation, informs stakeholders and authorizes the project manager to initiate (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.4).

n.0: 'Authorize the project' comes later: the board approves the PID, confirms project tolerances, commits resources and authorizes delivery (book Table 13.4).
n.1: 'Authorize a stage or exception plan' reviews the updated project dashboard and approves the updated release map at a stage boundary or after an exception (book Table 13.4).
n.3: 'Give ongoing direction' is informal guidance at any time in response to requests, escalated issues and exception reports, not the start of initiation (book Table 13.4).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: What is the main focus of the agile enablement workshop held as part of the 'directing a project' process?
o: Reviewing Agilometer assessments so that agile maturity and agile risks are assessed regularly
Reviewing completed features with users so that acceptance and feedback can be gathered
Selecting user stories for the next iteration based on their priority and estimated effort
Defining team OKRs and breaking key activities into user stories for the next stage
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: The agile enablement workshop holds regular Agilometer assessments so agile maturity and agile risks are assessed; its topics are Agilometer assessment review, risk identification, risk assessment and risk planning (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 13.3.3, Table 13.5).

n.1: Showing completed features to gather acceptance and feedback is the product demo topic of the progress review workshop (book Table 13.10).
n.2: Choosing stories by priority and estimate is the iteration planning topic of the team planning workshop (book Table 13.13).
n.3: Team OKRs and breaking activities into user stories belong to the release planning workshop at a stage boundary (book Table 13.16).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: In an agile enablement workshop, the board and agile coaches list further threats and opportunities to agile adoption that the Agilometer did not cover. Under which topic of the workshop does this belong?
o: Agilometer assessment review
Risk identification
Risk assessment
Risk planning
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: The risk identification topic captures additional threats and opportunities for agile adoption that are not covered by the Agilometer (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.5).

n.0: The Agilometer assessment review links the Agilometer's risk areas to agile values and transformation objectives; extra risks outside it are found under risk identification (book Table 13.5).
n.2: Risk assessment estimates probability and impact and prioritizes risks that have already been identified (book Table 13.5).
n.3: Risk planning agrees practical mitigation steps for the prioritized risks (book Table 13.5).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q:
Identify the missing words in the following sentence.

In the 'authorize a stage or exception plan' activity, the project board reviews the updated [?] and approves the updated release map, or instructs the project manager to close the project prematurely.
o: team dashboard
product backlog
end project report
project dashboard
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: When authorizing a stage or exception plan, the board reviews the updated project dashboard and approves the updated release map (and PID), or instructs premature closure (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.4).

n.0: Team dashboards report a team's progress to the project manager; the board works from the project dashboard (book Table 12.1).
n.1: The product backlog holds one team's user stories and is owned by the product owner; it is not what the board reviews to authorize a stage (book Table 13.4).
n.2: The end project report is approved by the board in 'authorize project closure', not when authorizing a stage or exception plan (book Table 13.4).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: Which of the following is part of the project board's 'authorize project closure' activity in PRINCE2 Agile?
o: Ensuring post-project benefits reviews and confirming the updated project canvas
Approving the project brief and the release map that will be used for initiation
Approving the PID, confirming project tolerances and committing the resources
Reviewing the updated project dashboard and approving the next release map update
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: In 'authorize project closure' the board compares the original and current PID, approves the end project report, ensures post-project benefits reviews cover the product in use and confirms the updated project canvas (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.4).

n.1: Approving the project brief and the release map for initiation is part of 'authorize initiation' (book Table 13.4).
n.2: Approving the PID, confirming tolerances and committing resources is part of 'authorize the project' (book Table 13.4).
n.3: Reviewing the updated project dashboard and approving the updated release map is part of 'authorize a stage or exception plan' (book Table 13.4).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: A board member of a pharmacy chain suggests that the organization's agile transformation plan should first be produced in the agile enablement workshop. Why does this not match PRINCE2 Agile guidance?
o: The plan is written by the agile coach in the starting up workshop, while the enablement workshop approves the project canvas
The plan is agreed in the release planning workshop, while the enablement workshop sets the team OKRs for each stage
The plan comes from the project initiation workshop, while the enablement workshop reviews Agilometer results and agile risks
The plan replaces the risk management approach, so it is approved by the board in the 'authorize the project' activity
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: The agile transformation plan is produced in initiation through the management approaches topic of the project initiation workshop, where it can replace the change management approach if needed; the agile enablement workshop reviews Agilometer assessments and agile adoption risks (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.7, Table 13.5).

n.0: The starting up workshop covers roles, lessons, initiation planning, risk and refine planning; the enablement workshop does not approve the project canvas (book Table 13.3, Table 13.5).
n.1: The release planning workshop defines team OKRs and updates the release map; the enablement workshop deals with Agilometer reviews and agile risks, not OKRs (book Table 13.16, Table 13.5).
n.3: The agile transformation plan can replace the change management approach, not the risk management approach (book Table 13.7).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: A building society has authorized initiation of its mortgage portal project. Which two named workshops does PRINCE2 Agile describe for the 'initiating a project' process?
o: The project initiation workshop and the project kickoff workshop
The project canvas workshop and the starting up workshop
The agile enablement workshop and the progress review workshop
The release planning workshop and the team planning workshop
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: In initiating a project the project manager defines participants for the project initiation workshop and the project kickoff workshop, sets dates and invites everyone (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 13.4.3, 13.4.4.1, 13.4.4.2).

n.1: The project canvas and starting up workshops support starting up a project, before initiation is authorized (book 13.2.3).
n.2: The agile enablement workshop supports directing a project and the progress review workshop supports controlling a stage (book 13.3.3, 13.5.4.1).
n.3: The release planning workshop supports managing a stage boundary and the team planning workshop supports managing product delivery (book 13.7.4.1, 13.6.4.1).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: During the project kickoff workshop for a council's waste collection app, each team maps its members' skills to find gaps and overlaps. Which kickoff topic is this?
o: Team delegation matrix
Team values and norms
Team skill matrix
Psychological safety
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: The team skill matrix topic maps the team's skills and shows gaps and overlaps (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.8).

n.0: The team delegation matrix simplifies decision-making and empowers self-management by making clear who decides what (book Table 13.8).
n.1: Team values and norms creates an agile culture and manages expectations for working together (book Table 13.8).
n.3: The psychological safety topic assesses how safe people feel to speak up and take part; it does not map skills (book Table 13.8).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: In the 'initiating a project' process, the project manager carries out the 'prepare the full business case' activity. What does this activity produce in PRINCE2 Agile?
o: A product backlog of user stories for each team
A more detailed version of the project canvas
A project dashboard for the board to pull data from
The project Definition of Ready and Definition of Done
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: In PRINCE2 Agile the full business case prepared during initiation is a more detailed project canvas (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.6).

n.0: Product backlogs of user stories are owned by product owners and hold each team's requirements; the full business case is a more detailed project canvas (book Table 13.6).
n.2: The project dashboard replaces the highlight report and is created in the project kickoff workshop, not as the business case (book Table 13.8, Table 12.1).
n.3: The project Definition of Ready and Definition of Done are topics of the project initiation workshop, not the output of preparing the full business case (book Table 13.7).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: In the project initiation workshop for a ferry operator's booking project, participants agree product-overarching criteria that a piece of work must meet before a team may start on it. Which topic of the workshop is this?
o: Project Definition of Done
Management approaches
Persona definition
Project Definition of Ready
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: The project Definition of Ready topic sets product-overarching criteria that must be met before work can start (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.7).

n.0: The project Definition of Done sets the criteria for work to be acceptable to users and the CPO, which applies when work is finished, not before it starts (book Table 13.7).
n.1: The management approaches topic co-creates structured yet flexible approaches; readiness criteria belong to the project Definition of Ready topic (book Table 13.7).
n.2: Persona definition describes fictional, needs-based users; it does not set criteria for starting work (book Table 13.7).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: A project manager wants the board to be able to pull up-to-date project information from the start of delivery. In PRINCE2 Agile, in which workshop is the project dashboard created?
o: The progress review workshop
The project initiation workshop
The agile enablement workshop
The project kickoff workshop
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: The project dashboard is a topic of the project kickoff workshop in initiating a project, where it is created (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.8).

n.0: The progress review workshop reviews project dashboard metrics during controlling a stage; the dashboard has already been created at kickoff (book Table 13.10, Table 13.8).
n.1: The project initiation workshop covers the Agilometer, management approaches, project DoR and DoD, personas, release planning and canvas refinement, not the dashboard (book Table 13.7).
n.2: The agile enablement workshop reviews Agilometer results and agile risks with the board; it does not create the project dashboard (book Table 13.5).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q:
Which two statements about the project initiation workshop are correct?

1. Team dashboards are designed by the project manager and then issued to each team.
2. Each participant assesses the Agilometer and the results are combined into one.
3. Team OKRs for the first iteration are defined under the persona definition topic.
4. If needed, the change management approach can be replaced by the agile transformation plan.
o: 1 and 2
2 and 4
1 and 3
3 and 4
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: Statement 2 describes the Agilometer topic and statement 4 the management approaches topic of the project initiation workshop (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.7).

n.0: Statement 1 is wrong: team dashboards are co-created by each team in the kickoff workshop, not designed by the project manager (book Table 13.8).
n.2: Both are wrong: team dashboards are co-created by teams (book Table 13.8), and OKRs are defined in the release planning workshop, not under persona definition (book Table 13.16).
n.3: Statement 3 is wrong: persona definition describes fictional users; team OKRs are defined in the release planning workshop (book Table 13.7, Table 13.16).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: Before the project kickoff workshop, a project manager designs a standard team dashboard and plans to require every delivery team to use it. Why does this conflict with PRINCE2 Agile guidance?
o: Team dashboards replace the highlight report, so the project board should design them for teams
Team dashboards are agreed in the release planning workshop at the end of the initiation stage
Team dashboards should be co-created by each team, supporting transparency and self-management
Team dashboards are created by project support in controlling a stage, after the first iteration
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: The kickoff workshop aims to build teamwork and an agile culture of openness and self-management; its team dashboards topic has each team co-create its own dashboard rather than having one dictated (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 13.4.4.2, Table 13.8).

n.0: Team dashboards replace the checkpoint report; it is the project dashboard that replaces the highlight report (book Table 12.1).
n.1: Team dashboards are a topic of the project kickoff workshop in initiating a project; the release planning workshop covers OKRs and the release map (book Table 13.8, Table 13.16).
n.3: Team dashboards are co-created by the teams at kickoff; project support helps update and pull information from dashboards later but does not create them (book Table 13.8, Table B.1).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: At the end of initiation, a project manager shares the final project canvas, the PID and the release map with the project board. Which initiating activity is this, and which board activity normally follows?
o: Request project authorization, followed by 'authorize the project'
Prepare the project plan, followed by 'authorize a stage or exception plan'
Request project authorization, followed by 'authorize initiation'
Establish project controls, followed by 'give ongoing direction'
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: In 'request project authorization' the project manager shares the final project canvas, PID and release map with the board; the board then approves the PID, confirms tolerances and commits resources in 'authorize the project' (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.6, Table 13.4).

n.1: 'Prepare the project plan' documents the release map and plans transition to operations; it is not the request to the board, and the board's next step is not a stage authorization (book Table 13.6, Table 13.4).
n.2: The activity is right but 'authorize initiation' happened earlier, when the board approved the project brief and the release map for initiation (book Table 13.4).
n.3: 'Establish project controls' sets stage boundaries, tolerances and escalation procedures; the board's response to the PID is 'authorize the project' (book Table 13.6, Table 13.4).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: In the 'controlling a stage' process, several activities need no dedicated agile event. Which named workshop does PRINCE2 Agile use for the 'evaluate stage status' activity?
o: The team retrospective workshop
The progress review workshop
The release planning workshop
The agile enablement workshop
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: Evaluating stage status takes place in a progress review; activities such as authorizing a work package, escalating issues and risks and taking corrective action need no dedicated agile event (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.9, 13.5.4.1).

n.0: The team retrospective workshop belongs to managing product delivery and reflects on the last iteration (book 13.6.4.2).
n.2: The release planning workshop belongs to managing a stage boundary and plans the next stage (book 13.7.4.1).
n.3: The agile enablement workshop belongs to directing a project and reviews Agilometer results with the board (book 13.3.3).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: During a progress review workshop for an airport's baggage-tracking project, the teams show newly completed features to users to gather their acceptance and feedback. Which topic of the progress review workshop is this?
o: Product demo
Project highlights
Current risks and issues
Wrap-up
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: The product demo topic shows completed features and gathers user acceptance and feedback (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.10).

n.1: Project highlights reviews the metrics on the project dashboard rather than demonstrating features (book Table 13.10).
n.2: Current risks and issues discusses open risks and issues and how to address them, not completed features (book Table 13.10).
n.3: Wrap-up closes the workshop by summarizing outcomes; it is not where features are demonstrated (book Table 13.10).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: In the 'report highlights' activity, the project manager assembles the team dashboards, the project log and changes to the release map. What does the project manager then update so that the board can pull the information it needs?
o: The team dashboard
The team's product backlog
The project canvas
The project dashboard
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: In 'report highlights' the project manager updates the project dashboard so that the board can pull information; the project dashboard replaces the highlight report (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.9, Table 12.1).

n.0: Team dashboards are one of the sources the project manager assembles; they report team progress to the project manager, not to the board (book Table 12.1).
n.1: The product backlog holds a team's user stories and is maintained by the product owner; in 'report highlights' the project manager updates the project dashboard, not a backlog (book Table 13.9).
n.2: The project canvas is the agile form of the business case; it is not updated as the regular progress report for the board (book 6.3.2.1, Table 13.9).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: What is the purpose of the progress review workshop in the 'controlling a stage' process?
o: To prepare for the next iteration by refining, estimating and selecting user stories
To build shared understanding of objectives and plan the next stage with team OKRs
To assess the project's current status, celebrate achievements and address any challenges
To confirm the final product meets requirements and prepare for handover to operations
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: The progress review workshop assesses current status, celebrates achievements and addresses challenges using metrics, accomplishments and open risks (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 13.5.4.1).

n.0: Preparing the next iteration is the purpose of the team planning workshop in managing product delivery (book 13.6.4.1).
n.1: Planning the next stage with OKRs is the purpose of the release planning workshop at a stage boundary (book 13.7.4.1).
n.3: Confirming the final product and preparing handover is the purpose of the project closure workshop (book 13.8.4).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: In the 'authorize a work package' activity of controlling a stage, with whom does the project manager co-create and review the work package description before work is authorized?
o: The chief product owner and the project executive
Project assurance and the senior supplier
The product owner and the delivery team
Project support and the agile coach
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: When authorizing a work package, the project manager co-creates and reviews the work package description with the product owner and the team, confirms acceptance and authorizes the work (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.9).

n.0: The CPO and executive work at project level; agreeing a work package is between the project manager, the product owner and the team (book Table 13.9).
n.1: Project assurance monitors independently and the senior supplier sits at board level; neither co-creates the work package description (book Table 13.9).
n.3: Project support helps with administration and the agile coach supports adoption across the organization; neither co-creates the work package description (book Table 13.9).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q:
Which two statements about the activities of the 'controlling a stage' process are correct?

1. In 'escalate issues and risks', the project manager recommends options to the board in an exception report.
2. Every activity of the process needs its own dedicated agile workshop.
3. In 'receive completed work package', the board confirms the set of user stories was delivered.
4. In 'evaluate work package status', the project manager pulls progress from the team dashboard.
o: 1 and 2
2 and 3
3 and 4
1 and 4
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: Statement 1 describes 'escalate issues and risks' and statement 4 describes 'evaluate work package status' (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.9).

n.0: Statement 2 is wrong: the book places 'evaluate stage status' in a progress review and says activities such as authorizing a work package or taking corrective action need no dedicated agile event (book Table 13.9).
n.1: Both are wrong: activities such as authorizing a work package need no dedicated agile event, and it is the project manager, not the board, who receives completed work packages (book Table 13.9).
n.2: Statement 3 is wrong: 'receive completed work package' is a project manager activity in controlling a stage, not a board decision (book Table 13.9).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q:

o: team building

the good
wrap-up

n.2: The good recognizes what went well and celebrates it; strengthening relationships through a shared activity is team building (book Table 13.11).
n.3: Wrap-up closes the session by summarizing what was agreed (book Table 13.11).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: Midway through a stage, a project manager forecasts that the remaining Must have features cannot be delivered within the stage's tolerances. Which action matches the 'escalate issues and risks' activity in PRINCE2 Agile?
o: Raise the slippage at the next progress review and record it on the team dashboards until the stage ends
Examine the release map, assess options against the canvas and release map, and recommend one in an exception report
Ask the delivery teams to extend the current iteration until all the remaining Must have features are complete
Update the project dashboard with a revised stage end date and wait for the board's review at the next stage boundary

n.0: A forecast breach of stage tolerance is an exception that must be escalated to the board in an exception report, not held until the stage ends (book Table 13.9, Table 12.1).
n.2: Time has zero tolerance by default and timeboxes are not extended; the forecast breach goes to the board as an exception (book Table 3.1, Table 13.9).
n.3: Changing the end date flexes time, which normally has zero tolerance, and waiting for the stage boundary delays the exception report the board needs (book Table 3.1, Table 13.9).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: A delivery team at an energy supplier is working on its part of a customer portal project. Which two named workshops support the 'managing product delivery' process in PRINCE2 Agile?
o: The progress review workshop and the project retrospective workshop

n.0: The progress review and project retrospective workshops support controlling a stage (book 13.5.4.1, Table 13.11).
n.1: The release planning workshop supports managing a stage boundary and the agile enablement workshop supports directing a project (book 13.7.4.1, 13.3.3).
n.3: The project initiation and project kickoff workshops support initiating a project (book 13.4.4.1, 13.4.4.2).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: In a team planning workshop, a product owner and developers make sure each story's acceptance criteria are clear and testable and agree what counts as done. Which topic of the team planning workshop is this?
o: Product backlog refinement
Effort estimation
Iteration planning
User story refinement

n.0: Product backlog refinement clarifies and prioritizes the backlog items using MoSCoW, rather than refining each story's acceptance criteria (book Table 13.13).
n.1: Effort estimation builds a shared view of the complexity and effort of each story (book Table 13.13).
n.2: Iteration planning selects stories by priority and estimate to form a realistic team plan (book Table 13.13).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: In the 'accept a work package' activity of managing product delivery, who produces the team plan showing what can be completed within the agreed constraints?
o: The delivery team
The project manager
The chief product owner
Project support

n.1: The project manager agrees the work package with the product owner and team but does not produce the team plan; detailed planning is the team's (book Table 13.9, Table 13.12).
n.2: The CPO prioritizes across teams at project level; the team plan for a work package is produced by the delivery team (book Table 13.12).
n.3: Project support provides administrative help; it does not produce team plans (book Table 13.12).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: In a team retrospective workshop, a delivery team discusses the problems, risks and challenges it met in the last iteration and what caused them. Which topic of the team retrospective workshop is this?
o: The learning
The bad
The good
Team building

n.0: The learning turns reflection into lessons, improvement suggestions and actionable insights, rather than listing the problems and causes (book Table 13.14).
n.2: The good recognizes what went well and celebrates it (book Table 13.14).
n.3: Team building uses a game or food to strengthen bonds within the team (book Table 13.14).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: In the 'evaluate a work package' activity, a delivery team reviews its registers and logs. Which artifact does the team then update so that the project manager can pull up-to-date information?
o: The project dashboard
The team dashboard
The release map
The project canvas
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: When evaluating a work package, the team reviews registers and logs and updates the team dashboard, from which the project manager pulls information (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.12, Table 12.1).

n.0: The project dashboard is updated by the project manager for the board in 'report highlights', not by the team in managing product delivery (book Table 13.9).
n.2: The release map is updated by the project manager with actuals and forecasts in controlling a stage (book Table 13.9).
n.3: The project canvas is the agile business case, maintained at project level; the team updates its team dashboard, not the canvas (book 6.3.2.1, Table 13.12).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q:
Which two statements about the team planning workshop are correct?

1. It reviews Agilometer results with the project board and agile coaches.
2. It defines team OKRs and updates the release map for the next stage.

o: 3 and 4
1 and 2
1 and 3
2 and 4
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: Statement 3 gives the purpose of the team planning workshop and statement 4 describes its iteration planning topic (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 13.6.4.1, Table 13.13).

n.1: Both are wrong: Agilometer reviews with the board belong to the agile enablement workshop, and team OKRs to the release planning workshop (book 13.3.3, Table 13.16).
n.2: Statement 1 is wrong: Agilometer reviews with the board and agile coaches take place in the agile enablement workshop (book 13.3.3).
n.3: Statement 2 is wrong: team OKRs and release map updates for the next stage belong to the release planning workshop (book Table 13.16).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: At the end of an iteration, a tester suggests a change to the way stories are handed from developers to testing so that less rework is needed next time. Under which topic of the team retrospective workshop does this suggestion belong?
o: The bad
The good
Team building
The learning

n.1: The good recognizes and celebrates what went well; it does not hold improvement proposals (book Table 13.14).
n.2: Team building strengthens bonds through a game or food, not through process changes (book Table 13.14).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: Where does PRINCE2 Agile place the detailed, task-level planning of the work for the next iteration?
o: In managing a stage boundary, during the release planning workshop
In controlling a stage, during the progress review workshop
In managing product delivery, during the team planning workshop
In initiating a project, during the project initiation workshop
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: Detailed planning happens in managing product delivery, where the team planning workshop refines and estimates stories and plans the next iteration; stage boundaries produce high-level release map updates (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 13.6.4.1, 13.7.4.1).

n.0: The release planning workshop at a stage boundary works at release map level, breaking key activities into user stories for the next stage, not detailed iteration tasks (book 13.7.4.1).
n.1: The progress review workshop assesses status, demonstrates features and addresses challenges; it does not plan the next iteration (book 13.5.4.1).
n.3: The project initiation workshop produces a high-level release map and management approaches, not iteration-level plans (book 13.4.4.1).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: A charity's donor app project is approaching the end of its initiation stage, and the project manager is preparing for the next stage. Which named workshop supports the 'managing a stage boundary' process?
o: The team planning workshop
The progress review workshop
The project closure workshop
The release planning workshop
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: Managing a stage boundary is supported by the release planning workshop, held for initiation and for subsequent stages, which plans the next stage (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 13.7.3, 13.7.4.1).

n.0: The team planning workshop supports managing product delivery and prepares the next iteration, not the next stage (book 13.6.4.1).
n.1: The progress review workshop supports controlling a stage by assessing the current status (book 13.5.4.1).
n.2: The project closure workshop supports closing a project in the final stage (book 13.8.4).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: In a release planning workshop for a rail operator's timetable project, each team defines or updates the objectives and measurable key results that will guide its work in the next stage. Which topic of the workshop is this?
o: Release planning
Introduction
OKR definition
Wrap-up
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: The OKR definition topic of the release planning workshop defines or updates team OKRs (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.16).

n.0: The release planning topic breaks key activities into user stories and updates the release map, rather than setting objectives and key results (book Table 13.16).
n.1: The introduction opens the workshop and sets the context for the session; OKRs are set under OKR definition (book Table 13.16).
n.3: Wrap-up closes the workshop by confirming outcomes; it is not where OKRs are defined (book Table 13.16).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: What is the purpose of the release planning workshop in the 'managing a stage boundary' process?
o: To prepare a delivery team for its next iteration by refining, estimating and selecting stories
To build shared understanding of objectives, align teams with the vision and plan the next stage
To assess agile maturity and agile risks with the board, agile coaches and business representatives
To formally conclude the project, confirm the final product and prepare for handover to operations
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: The release planning workshop builds shared understanding of objectives, aligns teams with the vision and plans the next stage, reviewing the project canvas, project backlog and release map (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 13.7.4.1).

n.0: Preparing the next iteration is the purpose of the team planning workshop in managing product delivery (book 13.6.4.1).
n.2: Assessing agile maturity and risks with the board is the purpose of the agile enablement workshop in directing a project (book 13.3.3).
n.3: Formally concluding the project is the purpose of the project closure workshop (book 13.8.4).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: Which artifacts are reviewed in the release planning workshop when the next stage is being planned?
o: The project canvas, the project backlog and the release map
The team dashboards, the iteration team plans and the skill matrix
The personas, the project Definition of Ready and the delegation matrix
The final product demo, the lessons report and the handover plan
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: The release planning workshop reviews the project canvas, the project backlog and the release map to plan the next stage (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 13.7.4.1).

n.1: Team dashboards and team plans are reviewed at team level in managing product delivery, and the skill matrix is a kickoff topic (book Table 12.1, Table 13.8).
n.2: Personas and the project Definition of Ready are project initiation workshop topics, and the delegation matrix is a kickoff topic (book Table 13.7, Table 13.8).
n.3: The final product demo, lessons report and handover planning are topics of the project closure workshop (book Table 13.19).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: In the 'prepare the next stage plan' activity of managing a stage boundary, what does the project manager update in PRINCE2 Agile?
o: The release map for the next stage, applying lessons and updating PID components
The team plan for each iteration of the next stage, on behalf of the teams
The team dashboards, so that each team reports in the same standard format
The project canvas workshop outputs, by repeating the workshop with the executive
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: Preparing the next stage plan reviews and updates PID components, applies lessons and updates the release map for the next stage, since the release map is the agile form of the stage plan (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.15, ch 8).

n.1: Team plans are produced by the delivery teams in managing product delivery; the stage boundary works at release map level (book Table 13.12).
n.2: Team dashboards are co-created and updated by each team; imposing one format conflicts with self-management (book Table 13.8).
n.3: The project canvas workshop belongs to starting up a project; it is not repeated to prepare the next stage plan (book 13.2.4.1).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q:
Which two statements about the release planning workshop are correct?

3. In its release planning topic, key activities are broken into user stories and the release map is updated.

o: 1 and 2
2 and 3
1 and 4
3 and 4
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: Statement 2 matches the release planning workshop for initiation, which plans the next stage, and statement 3 describes its release planning topic (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 13.7.4.1, Table 13.16).

n.0: Statement 1 is wrong: selecting stories for the next iteration is iteration planning in the team planning workshop (book Table 13.13).
n.2: Both are wrong: iteration-level story selection is team planning (book Table 13.13), and the project manager arranges the workshop (book 13.7.3).
n.3: Statement 4 is wrong: the project manager defines participants, sets dates and invites everyone to the release planning workshop (book 13.7.3).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q:

In PRINCE2 Agile, the end stage report that the board receives at a stage boundary is replaced by the [?].
o: team dashboard
release map
project dashboard
end project report

n.1: The release map replaces the project and stage plans, not the end stage report (book ch 8).
n.3: The end project report is a separate report produced when closing the project, reviewing performance against the PID; it is kept in PRINCE2 Agile and does not replace the end stage report (book Table 12.1).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: As a stage draws to a close, who defines the participants for the release planning workshop, sets its dates and invites everyone, and in which process does this take place?
o: The project executive, in directing a project
The team coach, in managing product delivery

The project manager, in managing a stage boundary

n.1: The team coach facilitates team-level workshops in managing product delivery; the release planning workshop belongs to the stage boundary (book 13.7.3).
n.2: The CPO takes part in planning, but the workshop belongs to managing a stage boundary and is arranged by the project manager (book 13.7.3).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: A museum's online ticketing project is in its final stage and the product is ready to hand over. Which named workshop supports the 'closing a project' process in PRINCE2 Agile?
o: The project closure workshop
The progress review workshop
The release planning workshop
The project retrospective workshop

n.1: The progress review workshop supports controlling a stage; the closure workshop does contain a progress review topic, but the named workshop is the project closure workshop (book 13.5.4.1, Table 13.19).
n.2: The release planning workshop supports managing a stage boundary and plans the next stage, which does not exist at closure (book 13.7.4.1).
n.3: The project retrospective workshop is used in controlling a stage; closing uses the project closure workshop (book Table 13.11, 13.8.4).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: What is the purpose of the project closure workshop in PRINCE2 Agile?
o: To review the current stage, update the release map and plan the work of the next stage with OKRs
To formally conclude the project by confirming the product meets requirements and preparing handover
To review the Agilometer with the board so that the risks of agile working can be reassessed
To demonstrate new features and celebrate achievements before the next set of iterations begins
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: The project closure workshop formally concludes the project: it confirms the final product meets requirements, reflects on lessons, finalizes documentation and prepares the handover to operations (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 13.8.4).

n.0: Planning the next stage with OKRs and the release map is the purpose of the release planning workshop at a stage boundary (book 13.7.4.1).
n.2: Reviewing the Agilometer with the board is the focus of the agile enablement workshop in directing a project (book 13.3.3).
n.3: Demonstrating features and celebrating achievements during a stage describes the progress review workshop (book 13.5.4.1).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: In the project closure workshop for a dental practice group's patient app, participants agree who will provide support after go-live, the operational requirements and the remaining benefits actions. Which topic of the workshop is this?
o: Final product demo
Current risks and issues
Final handover planning
Project lessons
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: Final handover planning agrees support responsibilities, operational requirements and the actions needed for benefits (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.19).

n.0: The final product demo shows the finished product to gain user acceptance and confirm it is ready for handover (book Table 13.19).
n.1: Current risks and issues is a topic of the progress review workshop in controlling a stage, not of the project closure workshop (book Table 13.10, Table 13.19).
n.3: Project lessons shares insights from the project; it does not agree support responsibilities (book Table 13.19).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: In the 'closing a project' process, which activity compares the project with the original PID and approved changes and produces the end project report and the lessons report?
o: Confirm project acceptance
Prepare planned closure
Request project closure
Evaluate the project

n.0: 'Confirm project acceptance' records follow-on action recommendations, checks post-project benefits arrangements and confirms handover (book Table 13.18).
n.1: 'Prepare planned closure' identifies who needs to know, updates the project log and release map with final actuals and drafts the closure notification (book Table 13.18).
n.2: 'Request project closure' sends the board a performance summary, confirmation of readiness and any concessions for off-specifications (book Table 13.18).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: The lessons report topic of the project closure workshop should capture actionable lessons. Which assessments' insights and trends does PRINCE2 Agile say this topic should include?
o: Velocity and burn-down chart assessments
Persona and Definition of Ready assessments
Skill matrix and delegation matrix assessments
Agilometer and psychological safety assessments
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: The lessons report topic includes insights and trends from the Agilometer and psychological safety assessments (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.19).

n.0: Velocity and burn-down charts track delivery progress; the closure workshop's lessons report names Agilometer and psychological safety trends (book Table 13.19).
n.1: Personas and the project Definition of Ready are set in the project initiation workshop; they are not the assessments named for the lessons report (book Table 13.7, Table 13.19).
n.2: The skill and delegation matrices are kickoff workshop topics; the lessons report names Agilometer and psychological safety trends (book Table 13.8, Table 13.19).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q:
Which two statements about closing a project in PRINCE2 Agile are correct?

3. In 'prepare planned closure', the project log and release map are updated with final actuals.
4. Most of the project's benefits are confirmed during the final product demo, before handover.
o: 1 and 2
2 and 4
1 and 3
3 and 4
