n.0: Statement 2 is wrong: closing a project is the last part of the final stage, not a stage of its own (PRINCE2 7 manual, ch 19).
n.1: Both are wrong: closing is part of the final stage, and most benefits are confirmed after closure through post-project benefits reviews (book 6.3.1, Table 13.4).
n.3: Statement 4 is wrong: most benefits are realized and confirmed after the project closes, which is why post-project benefits reviews are planned (book 6.3.1).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: During the project closure workshop, participants bring the PID, the logs, the project dashboard and the Agilometer up to date. Which topic of the project closure workshop is this?
o: Lessons report
Progress review
Project lessons
Final handover planning
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: In the project closure workshop, the progress review topic updates the PID, logs, project dashboard and Agilometer (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.19).

n.0: The lessons report topic uses these updates to produce actionable lessons; it is not where the PID, logs and dashboard are updated (book Table 13.19).
n.2: Project lessons shares insights gained during the project, rather than updating the project's records (book Table 13.19).
n.3: Final handover planning agrees support responsibilities, operational requirements and benefits actions (book Table 13.19).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: In closing a project, the project manager records follow-on action recommendations for unfinished work, open issues and risks, and confirms that the product has been handed over to operations. Which activity is this?
o: Confirm project acceptance
Authorize project closure
Request project closure
Prepare planned closure
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: 'Confirm project acceptance' covers follow-on action recommendations for unfinished work, issues and risks, checks that the benefits management approach includes post-project confirmation and confirms handover to operations (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.18).

n.1: 'Authorize project closure' is the board's activity in directing a project, where it approves the end project report and confirms the updated project canvas; the project manager's work described here belongs to closing a project (book Table 13.4, Table 13.18).
n.2: 'Request project closure' asks the board to close, with a performance summary, readiness and concessions for off-specifications (book Table 13.18).
n.3: 'Prepare planned closure' updates the project log and release map with final actuals and drafts the closure notification (book Table 13.18).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: A software firm moves its new payroll product from a project into agile product management. Which statement best describes how the product roadmap is treated in agile product management?
o: It is fixed when the product is launched so that development effort stays aligned with the original product vision
It is owned by the delivery team and replaces the product vision as the main guide for development decisions
It supports a high-level product vision and is adjusted as feedback from stakeholders, customers and the market arrives
It sets out every feature in detail with committed release dates for the coming year to give stakeholders certainty
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: Agile product managers keep a high-level product vision and align development with it through a flexible roadmap that is continually adjusted from stakeholder, customer and market feedback (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 14.2.2.1).

n.0: The roadmap in agile product management is flexible, not fixed at launch; it changes as feedback and market conditions change (book 14.2.2.1).
n.1: The roadmap serves the product vision rather than replacing it, and the product manager maintains them with the team (book 14.2.2.1).
n.3: Detailed long-range commitments contradict the flexible, continually adjusted roadmap described for agile product management (book 14.2.2.1).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: After an agile project delivers a new booking app and closes, users keep asking for enhancements. How does PRINCE2 Agile suggest these enhancements are best handled?
o: Through ongoing product management iterations, prioritized by business value, user feedback and market needs
By starting a new project for each enhancement so that each one has its own business case and board
By freezing all changes until the post-project benefits review has confirmed the original benefits
By passing every request to the chief product owner to decide and plan centrally for the next year
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: Agile product management uses short development cycles in which features and improvements are prioritized by business value, user feedback and evolving market needs, so enhancements go through product iterations rather than new projects (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 14.2.2.1).

n.1: Setting up a new project for each enhancement is not the approach described; agile product management delivers enhancements through iterations (book 14.2.2.1).
n.2: Holding back changes until a benefits review conflicts with the iterative planning, feedback and adaptation of agile product management (book 14.2.2.1).
n.3: Agile product management relies on close collaboration with development, design and other stakeholders, not centralized control by one role (book 14.2.2.1).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: An agile product manager works closely with development, design and other stakeholders throughout the life of a ticketing product. According to PRINCE2 Agile, what is the main aim of this collaboration?
o: To transfer the product manager's prioritization decisions to the design team
To keep the product aligned with both business objectives and user needs
To reduce the number of releases so that each contains more new features
To replace feedback from real users with the views of internal specialists
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: Agile product managers collaborate closely with development, design and other stakeholders so that the product aligns with both business objectives and user needs (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 14.2.2.1).

n.0: The product manager keeps prioritizing with the team; collaboration is about alignment, not handing prioritization to design (book 14.2.2.1).
n.2: Agile product management favours short cycles in which each release adds value, not fewer and larger releases (book 14.2.2.1).
n.3: User feedback is central to prioritization in agile product management; collaboration does not replace it (book 14.2.2.1).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: When an agile project's product is transferred to the operations team, PRINCE2 Agile recommends handing over the project's agile artifacts and tools. What is the main purpose of doing this?
o: To give end users a quick-start guide to the main features of the new product
To define the service levels and maintenance schedules for the support teams
To set out the contacts and timelines for resolving operational issues quickly
To keep the ways of working aligned with agile practices after the transition
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: Handing over agile artifacts and tools effectively ensures continuity and alignment with agile practices once the product is in operations (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 14.2.1).

n.0: Quick-start guides, manuals and videos support user adoption alongside training; they are not the purpose of handing over agile artifacts (book 14.2.1).
n.1: Service levels and maintenance schedules belong in the step-by-step operational procedures, a separate part of the transition (book 14.2.1).
n.2: Contacts and timelines for issue resolution are the escalation pathways, which help knowledge transfer but are a separate measure (book 14.2.1).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: Six weeks after a new case management system goes into operational use, the service manager wants evidence of what users find difficult so that the product can keep improving. Which transition measure in PRINCE2 Agile is intended for this?
o: Step-by-step operational procedures covering configuration and maintenance
Regular feedback loops such as user surveys, retrospectives and structured check-ins
Escalation pathways that name the contacts and timelines for resolving issues
Tailored training sessions supported by manuals and short video tutorials
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: Regular feedback loops, such as user surveys, retrospectives and structured check-ins, collect actionable insights that drive ongoing improvement and allow adjustments after transition (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 14.2.1).

n.0: Operational procedures support smooth, consistent maintenance and set expectations; they do not gather user insights (book 14.2.1).
n.2: Escalation pathways help resolve operational issues and transfer knowledge; they are not designed to collect improvement insights (book 14.2.1).
n.3: Training, manuals and videos help users adopt the product; they do not collect feedback on what users find difficult (book 14.2.1).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: A project manager is preparing the operational procedures that will be handed over with a new warehouse system. Which content does PRINCE2 Agile suggest these step-by-step procedures cover?
o: The project canvas, the personas, the team OKRs and the latest Agilometer assessment
Burn-down charts, velocity history and the team plans from each completed iteration
The lessons log, the daily log and the issue register from the project's final stage
Configuration management, maintenance schedules, SLAs and troubleshooting guides
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: Operational procedures in an explicit, step-by-step format cover configuration management, maintenance schedules, applicable SLAs and troubleshooting guides, giving smooth, consistent maintenance (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 14.2.1).

n.0: These are project-level artifacts used to justify, plan and steer the project; they are not operational maintenance procedures (book 14.2.1).
n.1: Burn charts, velocity and team plans track project delivery; they do not tell operations staff how to run and maintain the product (book 14.2.1).
n.2: Logs and registers record the project's own management; they are not the step-by-step procedures for operations (book 14.2.1).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: Which statement best describes continuous agile development and operations as explained in PRINCE2 Agile?
o: A final project stage in which developers hand the product to operations and the delivery team disbands
A way of grouping changes into large, infrequent releases to reduce disruption to users in operations
Practices for rapid, automated delivery that keep the product deployable and improving with little manual effort
An approach in which operations staff test each release once all development work has been completed
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: Continuous agile development and operations is a set of practices for rapid, automated delivery of features, fixes and improvements, keeping the product always deployable and continually improved with minimal manual intervention (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 14.2.2.2).

n.0: It is not a closing stage; it operationalizes agile practices so delivery continues after the project, with development and operations working together (book 14.2.2.2).
n.1: It relies on small, frequent incremental releases, not large infrequent ones (book 14.2.2.2).
n.3: In DevOps, development, testing and operations collaborate closely rather than testing at the end in a separate phase (book 14.2.2.2).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: A digital team adopts Continuous Delivery for its online banking product and releases features and fixes to production in small, incremental changes. What is the main benefit of this, according to PRINCE2 Agile?
o: Fast feedback from real users, allowing a high degree of agility
Less need to monitor the product's performance in production
Separate development and operations phases with clear handoffs
Delayed user feedback until a complete set of features is ready
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: Continuous Delivery releases new features or fixes to production in small increments so the team gets fast feedback from real users, giving a high degree of agility in development and operations (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 14.2.2.2).

n.1: Monitoring in production (performance, user behaviour, system health) remains important and feeds back into development (book 14.2.2.2).
n.2: DevOps brings development, testing and operations together; it does not separate them into phases with handoffs (book 14.2.2.2).
n.3: The aim of small releases is to get user feedback quickly, not to wait for a complete feature set (book 14.2.2.2).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: A transport authority uses AI to analyse historical and real-time project data, forecasting whether the expected benefits will still line up with the timelines and budget and warning early of cost overruns. Which PRINCE2 principle does PRINCE2 Agile say this use of AI supports?
o: Learn from experience
Ensure continued business justification
Define roles, responsibilities and relationships
Tailor to suit the project
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: AI supports ensuring continued business justification by using predictive analytics to forecast whether anticipated benefits will align with projected timelines and budgets, and by flagging early signs of overruns (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 15.4.1).

n.0: AI supports learning from experience by turning large volumes of lessons into searchable, prioritized insights, not by forecasting viability (book 15.4.1).
n.2: AI supports defined roles, responsibilities and relationships by analysing skills and workload to suggest role assignments, not by forecasting viability (book 15.4.1).
n.3: AI supports tailoring by spotting similarities with past projects and suggesting how to adapt the method (book 15.4.1).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: An organization has years of lessons logs that nobody reads. It uses AI to categorize and prioritize the lessons, make them searchable by role and project stage, and highlight recurring issues and proven solutions. Which principle does this use of AI support?
o: Manage by exception
Define roles, responsibilities and relationships
Learn from experience
Manage by stages
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: AI strengthens learning from experience by turning large volumes of lessons into accessible, prioritized insights tailored to roles or stages, highlighting recurring issues and proven solutions (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 15.4.1).

n.0: Manage by exception is about delegating authority through tolerances; the AI use described here works on past lessons (book 5.2.1.5, 15.4.1).
n.1: AI supports defined roles by analysing skills and workload to suggest role assignments, not by organizing lessons (book 15.4.1).
n.3: AI supports manage by stages by adjusting predictions and refining the next stage or iteration plan (book 15.4.1).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: A project manager uses AI to analyse team members' skills, past performance and workload, suggest role assignments and flag gaps or overlaps in responsibilities. Which principle does PRINCE2 Agile link to this use of AI, and why?
o: Manage by exception, as it sets the tolerances within which each role may decide
Manage by stages, as it plans which people are needed in the next stage
Focus on products, as it links each team member to the products they will build
Define roles, responsibilities and relationships, as it makes clear who does what
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: AI supports defined roles, responsibilities and relationships by analysing data, skills and workload to suggest role assignments and highlight gaps or overlaps, improving role clarity (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 15.4.1).

n.0: Manage by exception concerns tolerances and delegated authority; analysing skills and workload to clarify roles supports defined roles (book 5.2.1.5, 15.4.1).
n.1: AI supports manage by stages by refining predictions for timelines, costs and benefits for the next stage or iteration, not by suggesting role assignments (book 15.4.1).
n.2: AI supports focus on products by helping define products, draft user stories and automate testing, not by assigning roles (book 15.4.1).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: A delivery team uses AI to help decompose the project product into smaller components, draft user stories from user needs, prioritize backlog items and run automated tests. Which principle does PRINCE2 Agile say this supports?
o: Focus on products
Ensure continued business justification
Manage by stages
Define roles, responsibilities and relationships
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: AI supports focus on products by helping define and decompose products, describe user stories based on user needs, prioritize backlogs and use automated testing to check quality (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 15.4.1).

n.1: AI supports continued business justification through forecasts of benefits against timelines and budgets, not product decomposition (book 15.4.1).
n.2: AI supports manage by stages by adjusting predictions and refining the next stage or iteration plans (book 15.4.1).
n.3: AI supports defined roles by suggesting role assignments from skills and workload data (book 15.4.1).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: According to PRINCE2 Agile, how can AI support communication within an agile project?
o: By automating routine information updates so leaders can focus on high-impact communication
By replacing face-to-face conversations with stakeholders on the progress of the project
By deciding which stakeholder messages the project board needs to approve before release
By removing the need to agree a communication management approach for the project
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: AI supports communication by automating the collection and dissemination of information and answering common questions through a project chatbot, freeing leaders for strategic, high-impact communication; it does not remove the need to communicate with stakeholders (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 15.4.2).

n.1: AI supports communication, but the need for people to communicate with stakeholders remains (book 15.4.2).
n.2: The book does not give AI a role in deciding which messages the board approves; communication decisions stay with people (book 15.4.2).
n.3: The communication management approach remains a PRINCE2 Agile product; AI helps carry out communication, it does not remove the approach (book 15.4.2).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: Which of the following is NOT described in PRINCE2 Agile as a way in which AI supports a project?
o: Spotting similarities with past projects to suggest how the method could be tailored
Highlighting gaps or overlaps in role responsibilities from skills and workload data
Refining time, cost and benefit predictions when planning the next iteration or stage
Taking over key project decisions so that the board no longer needs to make them
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: AI supports human decision-making with forecasts and insights, but it does not remove human decision-making; the board remains accountable for key decisions (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 15.4.2, 13.3.1).

n.0: This is described: AI can spot similarities with past projects and suggest tailoring and where agile practices fit best (book 15.4.1).
n.1: This is described: AI can analyse skills and workload to suggest role assignments and flag gaps or overlaps (book 15.4.1).
n.2: This is described: AI can adjust predictions and refine plans for the next iteration or stage, supporting manage by stages (book 15.4.1).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: Before initiation, a project office uses AI to compare a new project with similar past projects and suggest how the method should be adapted and where agile practices would fit best. Which principle does this use of AI support?
o: Manage by exception
Tailor to suit the project
Ensure continued business justification
Focus on products
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: AI supports tailoring by spotting similarities with past projects and suggesting tailoring options and where agile practices fit best (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 15.4.1).

n.0: Manage by exception is about tolerances and delegated authority, not about adapting the method (book 5.2.1.5).
n.2: AI supports continued business justification by forecasting whether benefits will align with timelines and budgets, not by suggesting how to adapt the method (book 15.4.1).
n.3: AI supports focus on products by helping define products and user stories and automate testing (book 15.4.1).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: PRINCE2 Agile describes several people-related uses of AI. Which of these describes how AI can support team leadership?
o: Scoring each team member's performance so that annual appraisals can be fully automated
Replacing team retrospectives with automated reports on the team's mood and engagement
Helping leaders understand team relationships, individual strengths and workload distribution
Selecting the user stories that each team must deliver in its next iteration on its behalf
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: AI can enhance team leadership by helping teams understand the complexity of team relationships, identifying individual strengths and tracking workload distribution (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 15.4.2).

n.0: Automated appraisal scoring is not a use the book describes; AI supports leaders but does not replace human judgement about people (book 15.4.2).
n.1: Team retrospectives remain a team workshop in managing product delivery; AI does not replace them (book 13.6.4.2, 15.4.2).
n.3: Selecting stories for the next iteration is the team's iteration planning in the team planning workshop, not a task handed to AI (book Table 13.13).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: A housing association has received a project mandate for a new tenant repairs app. Before any initiation work is authorized, the board wants to know whether there is a viable and worthwhile project at all. Which process has the purpose of answering this question?
o: Initiating a project
Starting up a project
Directing a project
Managing a stage boundary
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: Starting up a project makes sure the prerequisites for initiating are in place by answering whether there is a viable and worthwhile project; it is triggered by the project mandate (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 13.2.1).

n.0: Initiating a project comes after starting up; it lays solid foundations so the business understands the work before committing significant expenditure (book 13.4.1).
n.2: Directing a project lets the board stay accountable through key decisions; the question of whether there is a viable and worthwhile project is the purpose of starting up (book 13.3.1).
n.3: Managing a stage boundary gives the board information to review the current stage and approve the next stage plan; it is not where the first viability question is asked (book 13.7.1).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: Which statement describes the purpose of the 'initiating a project' process in PRINCE2 Agile?
o: To check that the prerequisites for initiation are in place by confirming the project is viable and worthwhile
To give the board enough information to review the current stage and approve the plan for the next stage
To control the link between the project manager and the delivery team for the delivery of specialist products
To establish solid foundations so the business understands the work needed before committing significant expenditure
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: Initiating a project establishes solid foundations so the business understands the work needed to deliver the project product before committing to significant expenditure (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 13.4.1).

n.0: This is the purpose of starting up a project, which comes before initiation and asks whether the project is viable and worthwhile (book 13.2.1).
n.1: This is the purpose of managing a stage boundary, which supports the board's review of each stage (book 13.7.1).
n.2: This is the purpose of managing product delivery, which links the project manager with the delivery team (book 13.6.1).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: A delivery team and its project manager agree the requirements for accepting, carrying out, reporting on and delivering a set of user stories. Which process has the purpose of controlling this link between the project manager and the delivery team?
o: Managing product delivery
Controlling a stage
Directing a project
Managing a stage boundary
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: Managing product delivery controls the link between the project manager and the delivery team by agreeing requirements for acceptance, execution, reporting and delivery of specialist products (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 13.6.1).

n.1: Controlling a stage is the project manager's process for assigning and monitoring work and keeping the stage within tolerances; the team side of the link is managing product delivery (book 13.5.1).
n.2: Directing a project is the board's process for key decisions and overall control; it does not manage the project manager's link with the delivery team (book 13.3.1).
n.3: Managing a stage boundary prepares information for the board's review of the stage and the next stage plan; it does not control work packages (book 13.7.1).

Agile: Processes & Wider Context.q: The board of a regional bus company wants to remain accountable for the success of its ticketing project while leaving day-to-day management to the project manager. Which process enables the board to do this through key decisions and overall control?
o: Controlling a stage
Starting up a project
Directing a project
Closing a project
Agile: Processes & Wider Context.w: Directing a project enables the project board to be accountable for the project's success by making key decisions and exercising overall control, while delegating day-to-day management to the project manager (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 13.3.1).

n.0: Controlling a stage is the project manager's process for day-to-day control of a stage within tolerances, not the board's process (book 13.5.1).
n.1: Starting up a project checks that the prerequisites for initiation are in place; it is not the board's ongoing means of control (book 13.2.1).
n.3: Closing a project provides a fixed point to confirm acceptance of the project product; it does not provide ongoing board control (PRINCE2 7 manual 19.1).
